q: Contoso adds contoso.com to its Microsoft 365 tenant. The DNS zone already contains an MX record pointing to the current third-party mail provider, an SPF record, and an Autodiscover CNAME. The domain still shows as unverified, and mail flow must not be disrupted during verification. What should you do?
opts: Add the TXT record value that Microsoft 365 generated for the domain
Change the MX record to point to the Exchange Online mail servers
Update the SPF record to include spf.protection.outlook.com
Point the Autodiscover CNAME at autodiscover.outlook.com
why: Ownership is proven only by the unique TXT verification value Microsoft 365 issues for that domain; publishing it has no effect on mail routing, so the current provider keeps working. Changing the MX record would cut mail over to Exchange Online before mailboxes exist there, which is the disruption the scenario rules out. Updating SPF and repointing Autodiscover are post-verification setup steps for sending and client configuration; neither proves ownership, so the domain would remain unverified.

q: Contoso's HR system sets the department attribute on every new Microsoft Entra user. All users in the Sales department must receive a Microsoft 365 E3 license on their first day, and license assignment must require no per-hire action by IT. Which should you configure?
opts: A dynamic security group with a department membership rule, with the license assigned to the group
An assigned security group with the license assigned to the group, with HR adding new hires to it
A dynamic distribution group for the Sales department, with the license assigned to the group
A scheduled PowerShell script that assigns the license to any user whose department is Sales
why: Group-based licensing on a dynamic security group means membership recalculates from the department attribute HR already populates, so the license follows automatically with no per-hire step. An assigned group still needs someone to add each new hire, which is exactly the manual action to avoid. A dynamic distribution group is an Exchange Online object, not a Microsoft Entra security group, so it cannot carry a license assignment. A scheduled script works but is custom code to maintain and runs on a delay, so it is more effort than the native feature.

q: Finance users receive Microsoft 365 E5 through group-based licensing on the Finance security group. Compliance requires that Finance users not use Viva Engage, while every other department keeps it. You need to meet the requirement with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
opts: Disable the Viva Engage service plan on the Finance group's license assignment
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks Viva Engage for the Finance group
Disable the Viva Engage service plan directly on each Finance user's account
Replace the group's Microsoft 365 E5 assignment with Office 365 E3 plus the missing add-ons
why: Service plans can be toggled per license assignment, so turning off Viva Engage on the Finance group's assignment removes it for every current and future member in one change while leaving other departments untouched. A Conditional Access block is an access workaround, not a licensing change, and leaves the users licensed for a service they are forbidden to use. Disabling the plan per user is repeated effort, and because the group assignment still enables the plan, a direct per-user disable does not take effect while the group grants it. Swapping SKUs is unnecessary churn and does not reproduce E5.

q: Contoso buys licenses through a Cloud Solution Provider partner. The partner must manage Exchange Online for the next 90 days. Contoso requires least privilege and does not want partner accounts created in its own directory. What should you do?
opts: Approve a granular delegated admin privileges relationship scoped to the Exchange Administrator role with a 90-day duration
Create a guest account for each partner engineer and make it eligible for Exchange Administrator in Privileged Identity Management
Accept a classic delegated admin privileges relationship and ask the partner to remove it after 90 days
Assign the partner a custom Microsoft Entra role that contains only Exchange permissions, scoped to an administrative unit
why: GDAP lets Contoso approve exactly the roles requested, for a set duration, and partner engineers use their own partner-tenant identities, so nothing is created in Contoso's directory. Guest accounts with PIM would achieve least privilege but create accounts in Contoso's tenant that must then be managed and removed. Classic DAP grants broad Admin Agent access with no expiration and relies on the partner to clean up. A custom Microsoft Entra role still has to be assigned to an identity inside Contoso's directory, and custom Entra roles cover directory permissions, not Exchange Online administration.

q: Contoso manages Microsoft 365 Apps with Intune. The IT pilot ring must receive new features as soon as Microsoft releases them. All other devices must receive new features once per month on a predictable date, with no additional feature delay. Which update channels should you assign to the pilot ring and to the other devices, respectively?
opts: Current Channel and Monthly Enterprise Channel
Beta Channel and Monthly Enterprise Channel
Current Channel (Preview) and Current Channel
Monthly Enterprise Channel and Current Channel
why: Current Channel delivers features as soon as they are ready, which fits the pilot ring, and Monthly Enterprise Channel bundles that month's features onto one predictable date (the second Tuesday), which fits everyone else. Beta Channel delivers pre-release builds that are not supported for production devices, and putting the other devices on Current Channel would give them features with no set schedule. Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel is no longer a slower option: since Version 2606 (July 2026) it receives the same monthly feature updates as Monthly Enterprise Channel. The Monthly Enterprise Channel and Current Channel pairing is reversed: it would give the pilot ring the predictable cadence and the broad population the unpredictable one.

q: Contoso's reception team needs a reception@contoso.com address. Five staff members must send as the address, and every reply must land in one common Inbox rather than in each person's own mailbox. No SharePoint site, calendar, or Planner should be provisioned, and no additional license should be consumed. What should you create?
opts: A shared mailbox
A distribution group
A Microsoft 365 group
A mail-enabled security group
why: A shared mailbox provides a single Inbox that delegated users open and send from with Send As permissions, needs no license under the size threshold, and provisions nothing else. A distribution group only fans mail out to each member's own mailbox, so there is no common Inbox for replies. A Microsoft 365 group would give a shared mailbox but also provisions a SharePoint site, calendar, and Planner, which the scenario excludes. A mail-enabled security group delivers to members like a distribution group and exists to grant permissions, not to hold mail.

q: Contoso routes all internet traffic, including Microsoft 365, through an on-premises proxy. Users report choppy audio in Teams calls. The network team confirms the proxy is not overloaded. According to Microsoft 365 network connectivity principles, what should you change?
opts: Let Optimize category endpoints, including Teams media, bypass the proxy and egress directly to the internet
Configure split tunneling so that only Default category endpoints bypass the proxy and egress directly
Enable QoS DSCP marking for Teams audio and video traffic on the internal corporate network
Change the Teams meeting policy so that media is carried over TCP instead of UDP
why: Microsoft's connectivity principles say Optimize endpoints, which carry latency-sensitive Teams media, should bypass proxies and VPNs and take the shortest path to Microsoft's network. Bypassing only the Default category is backwards: Default traffic is the low-priority bucket that can stay on the normal path. QoS marking helps prioritize media on congested internal links but does not remove the latency added by hairpinning through a proxy. Forcing TCP makes real-time media worse, since UDP is preferred for Teams calls.

q: Contoso assigns Current Channel to an IT pilot ring and Monthly Enterprise Channel to most users. Which two statements about this design are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Monthly Enterprise Channel devices receive that month's new features on a single predictable release date
Features reach Current Channel devices before they reach Monthly Enterprise Channel devices
Monthly Enterprise Channel devices receive security updates only every three months
Current Channel devices receive new features on a fixed monthly release date
why: Monthly Enterprise Channel bundles the month's features onto one release date (the second Tuesday), and it only includes features that have already rolled out in Current Channel, so Current Channel users have them first. Every channel still receives security updates monthly; three months is how long a Monthly Enterprise Channel version is supported, not its security update cadence. Current Channel ships features as soon as they are ready, which is why its cadence is less predictable than Monthly Enterprise Channel's.

q: Contoso's Cloud Solution Provider partner sends a granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) relationship request. Which two statements describe what Contoso is agreeing to if it approves it? (Choose two.)
opts: The partner receives only the Microsoft Entra roles listed in the request, for the duration specified
Partner staff gain access through their own partner-tenant identities rather than accounts created in Contoso's directory
The relationship automatically includes Global Administrator so the partner can recover the tenant
Contoso cannot end the relationship before its expiration date, because termination is controlled by the partner
why: A GDAP relationship is explicitly scoped to the roles named in the request and runs for a defined duration, and partner engineers are mapped to those roles through security groups in the partner's own tenant, so no accounts are created in Contoso's directory. Global Administrator is included only if the partner requests it and Contoso approves it; nothing is added automatically. Contoso can terminate a GDAP relationship at any time from the Microsoft 365 admin center, which is part of what distinguishes it from classic DAP.

q: An organization is migrating from Tenant A to Tenant B during a merger and wants to reuse its custom domain contoso.com in Tenant B. What must happen before contoso.com can be verified in Tenant B?
opts: Nothing; the same custom domain can be verified in both tenants at the same time
Remove the domain from Tenant A's verified domains, then add and verify it in Tenant B
Tenant B must be granted a GDAP relationship to Tenant A before the domain can be verified
A new TXT record must be published for Tenant A only, and Tenant B inherits verification automatically
why: A custom domain can only be verified in one Microsoft 365 tenant at a time, so it must be removed from the source tenant's verified domains before the destination tenant can add and verify it. Attempting to verify it in both tenants at once is not supported, which is why domain cutover is typically the last, carefully timed step of a tenant-to-tenant migration.

q: Contoso's service desk must be able to reset passwords for non-administrator users and open support requests with Microsoft. Service desk staff must not be able to reset passwords for users who hold admin roles or modify user accounts. You need to follow the principle of least privilege. Which role should you assign?
opts: Helpdesk Administrator
Password Administrator
User Administrator
Service Support Administrator
why: Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for non-admins (and other helpdesk admins), and it can also create and manage Microsoft support requests, which covers both duties with no account-editing rights. Password Administrator can reset non-admin passwords but cannot open support requests. User Administrator adds the ability to create and modify users and groups, which exceeds least privilege. Service Support Administrator can open support requests and view service health but cannot reset anyone's password.

q: The Message center in the Microsoft 365 admin center reports the real-time operational status of a service outage, while Service health announces upcoming feature changes.
opts: True
False
why: This has the two reversed: Service health reports real-time operational status and incidents, while Message center announces upcoming planned changes, new features, and deprecations admins need to plan for.

q: Contoso synchronizes its single Active Directory forest with Microsoft Entra Connect. It acquires Fabrikam, whose forest has no network connectivity or trust with Contoso's forest, and must bring Fabrikam users into the same tenant. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync agents can be installed in Fabrikam's forest and run alongside the existing Microsoft Entra Connect server
Cloud Sync does not require network line of sight from Contoso's Microsoft Entra Connect server to Fabrikam's domain controllers
A second active Microsoft Entra Connect server can be installed in Fabrikam's forest and pointed at the same tenant
A forest trust between Contoso and Fabrikam must be created before either tool can synchronize Fabrikam's users
why: Cloud Sync's lightweight agents install inside the forest they synchronize and are managed from the Microsoft Entra admin center, so they can cover Fabrikam's disconnected forest while Microsoft Entra Connect keeps handling Contoso's forest; the two tools are supported side by side for different forests. Only one active Microsoft Entra Connect server is supported per tenant (additional servers must be in staging mode), so a second active server is not an option. Neither tool requires a forest trust; Microsoft Entra Connect would need network connectivity to Fabrikam's domain controllers, which is exactly what is missing.

q: Contoso needs a group that project managers can email to reach all project leads, and that site owners can use to grant permissions on several SharePoint sites. The group must not provision its own mailbox, SharePoint site, or Planner. Which type of group should you create?
opts: A mail-enabled security group
A Microsoft 365 group
A distribution group
A security group
why: A mail-enabled security group is both a mail recipient and a security principal, so it can receive email and be used in SharePoint permission grants without provisioning any connected resources. A Microsoft 365 group would also satisfy email and permissions, but it automatically creates a group mailbox, SharePoint site, and Planner, which the scenario excludes. A distribution group receives email but is not a security principal, so it cannot be used to grant SharePoint permissions. A plain security group can be used for permissions but is not mail-enabled.

q: Contoso's legal team asks you to place the shared mailbox contracts@contoso.com on Litigation Hold. The mailbox is accessed only through delegates who hold Microsoft 365 E3 licenses, and no one signs in to it directly. An administrator states that shared mailboxes never require a license. What should you do?
opts: Assign an Exchange Online license to the shared mailbox before applying the hold
Apply the hold without a license, since no one signs in to the mailbox directly
Convert the shared mailbox to a user mailbox so the hold can be applied
Apply the hold to each delegate's mailbox instead, since their licenses cover the shared mailbox
why: A shared mailbox is license-free only while it stays under the size threshold with no archive, no hold, and no direct sign-in. Placing it on Litigation Hold is one of the conditions that requires an Exchange Online license on the shared mailbox itself. The 'no direct sign-in' rule covers normal delegated use, not holds. Converting to a user mailbox is unnecessary and still needs a license. Delegates' licenses never extend to the shared mailbox object, and holding their mailboxes would not preserve the shared mailbox's content.

q: Contoso publishes SPF and DKIM records for contoso.com. Attackers still send spoofed messages that appear to come from contoso.com, and some partner mail systems deliver them. Contoso wants receiving systems to reject messages that fail authentication and wants to receive aggregate reports about those failures. What should you publish?
opts: A DMARC TXT record with a reject policy and a reporting address
An SPF record that ends with a hard fail (-all) qualifier
A second DKIM selector with a longer signing key
An MX record that routes inbound mail through Exchange Online Protection
why: DMARC is the policy layer on top of SPF and DKIM: it tells receiving servers what to do on failure (monitor, quarantine, or reject) and where to send aggregate reports, which covers both requirements. A hard-fail SPF qualifier only signals a failed sender check; it provides no reporting and receivers treat it inconsistently. Another DKIM selector strengthens signing but does not instruct receivers about disposition. Changing the MX record affects how Contoso receives its own mail, not how other organizations handle mail spoofing contoso.com.

q: A new hire's account is created by an HR provisioning script that leaves the usage location attribute blank. The user is then added to a group that already carries a Microsoft 365 license through group-based licensing. What happens?
opts: The assignment fails and the user stays unlicensed until an administrator sets a usage location
The license is assigned, and the user is treated as located in the tenant's own location, which may be the wrong country for them
The system automatically copies the assigning admin's own usage location onto the account
The license is assigned, but only the services available worldwide are enabled until a usage location is set
why: For group-based licensing, a user with no usage location inherits the location of the tenant, so the license is assigned and no error appears, but services are provisioned for the tenant's country, which may be wrong for the user (and if that location is not supported, a 'Usage location isn't allowed' error appears). Assigning a license directly requires the usage location to be set first. Usage location matters for every license, not just Copilot, and nothing is copied from the admin's own account. The fix is to populate usage location in the provisioning flow.

q: An external auditor needs broad read-only visibility into nearly every Microsoft 365 admin center configuration setting, while a separate analyst only needs to view usage reports and nothing else. Which built-in roles fit the auditor and the analyst, respectively?
opts: Global Reader for the auditor; Reports Reader for the analyst
Reports Reader for the auditor; Global Reader for the analyst
Global Administrator for the auditor; Helpdesk Administrator for the analyst
User Administrator for both the auditor and the analyst
why: Global Reader mirrors Global Administrator's broad visibility but with no edit rights, suiting the auditor, while Reports Reader is scoped narrowly to usage reports, suiting the analyst. The reversed pairing is wrong, and Global Administrator or User Administrator would grant edit rights far beyond what either person needs.

q: A global company wants its European employees' primary mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint data to physically reside in an EU datacenter while North American employees' data stays in a North American datacenter, all inside one single Microsoft 365 tenant and directory. Which capability enables this?
opts: The EU Data Boundary
Multi-Geo
Customer Lockbox
Restricted SharePoint Search
why: Multi-Geo lets a single tenant place a given user's own data in a chosen satellite region while remaining one tenant and directory, matching this exact scenario. The EU Data Boundary instead governs whether an entire in-scope tenant's data stays within the EU/EFTA region, not per-user placement across multiple regions within one tenant.

q: A dynamic security group with the rule department -eq "Finance" is used for group-based licensing. When an administrator manually adds a contractor to that group, the contractor receives the group's license.
opts: True
False
why: Membership of a dynamic group is calculated entirely from its rule; members cannot be added or removed manually, so the attempt is not possible and no license results. To license the contractor, set the attribute the rule evaluates, add the contractor to a separate assigned group that also carries the license, or assign the license directly. The misconception is treating a dynamic group like an assigned group with a helpful default rule.

q: Contoso must prevent frontline workers from recording Teams meetings and must allow only executives to delete chat messages they have sent. Both settings must apply only to the relevant groups and must not change behavior for anyone else. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
opts: Create a meeting policy with cloud recording turned off and assign it to the frontline workers group
Create a messaging policy that allows deleting sent messages and assign it to the executives group
Turn off cloud recording in the Global (Org-wide default) meeting policy
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the Teams recording feature for frontline workers
why: Teams meeting policies control in-meeting capabilities such as recording, and messaging policies control chat behavior such as deleting sent messages; both can be assigned to a group so that only its members are affected. Changing the Global (Org-wide default) policy alters behavior for every user who has no custom policy, which violates the 'no one else' constraint. Conditional Access governs the conditions of sign-in and session, not individual Teams features such as recording.

q: An admin configures SSPR to require one authentication method to reset a password, and a user has registered two methods. The user then loses access to one of their two registered methods. What is the effect on their ability to reset their own password going forward?
opts: They can still reset their password using their one remaining registered method, since only one method is required at reset time
They can no longer use self-service password reset at all until both original methods are restored
Their account is automatically disabled until a helpdesk agent manually re-registers both methods
SSPR requires exactly the same number of methods at reset as at registration, so losing one method blocks all self-service reset
why: Registering more methods than a reset requires is deliberate — it gives a user more than one option to fall back on, so losing access to just one registered method still leaves them able to reset using the other. The reset step only requires the number of methods configured for reset (here one), not however many the user happened to register, and none of this disables the account automatically.

q: An organization wants every self-service-created Microsoft 365 group to automatically carry a department-based prefix, and wants group names containing a list of specific blocked terms to be rejected outright at creation time. Which feature should be configured?
opts: A Microsoft 365 Groups naming policy with a blocked words list
A Conditional Access policy scoped to the Groups creation experience
Entitlement management (access packages)
A Microsoft Entra dynamic group membership rule
why: A groups naming policy enforces a required prefix or suffix convention and a separate blocked words list that rejects disallowed terms at creation time, matching both requirements directly. Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions rather than naming, entitlement management governs requesting access to existing resources rather than group creation naming, and a dynamic group rule only controls automatic membership, not naming conventions.

q: Teams external access (federation) adds a user from another organization as a persistent member of a specific team, with ongoing access to that team's channels and files.
opts: True
False
why: That describes guest access, not external access. External access (federation) only lets users in separate tenants chat, call, and meet with each other without either becoming a member of the other tenant; persistent channel and file membership requires adding the user as an actual Entra B2B guest instead.

q: After a ransomware attack encrypts several hundred SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts, Contoso wants to return them to their state from yesterday morning at scale, and the work must be billed only for the data protected rather than per user. Which service fits?
opts: Microsoft 365 Backup, restoring the sites and accounts to a prior point in time
eDiscovery (Premium) with a hold, exporting the content back into the sites
Retention policies in Microsoft Purview, releasing the preserved copies from the Preservation Hold library
The SharePoint recycle bin, restoring every deleted item from the second-stage bin
why: Microsoft 365 Backup is built for large-scale recovery, rolling SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts back to a chosen earlier point in time, and it is metered by the data protected through pay-as-you-go billing. Retention policies preserve content for compliance, and recovering from the Preservation Hold library is a per-item, manual effort that does not restore sites to a point in time. The recycle bin holds deleted items, not encrypted or overwritten ones, and has no concept of rolling a whole site back. eDiscovery holds are for legal discovery, not for restoring a production site.

q: An admin is preparing to turn on Microsoft 365 Backup. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: Backup policies can only be created for Exchange mailboxes, because OneDrive and SharePoint use retention instead
The admin must hold the SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator role
Billing is pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription, so an Azure subscription with a resource group and region must be linked
Backup is included at no cost with every Microsoft 365 E5 license
why: Setup is done by a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator, and it needs a pay-as-you-go billing policy linked to an Azure subscription (with resource group and region) before backup policies are created. It is a metered service, not bundled with E5. Backup policies exist for OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange, so the claim that only mailboxes are supported is wrong.

q: Contoso's Sydney office reports slow Teams calls, while Service health shows no incidents. The admin wants evidence about the office's own network design before talking to the ISP. Where should they look?
opts: Message center, searching for upcoming Teams media changes that might have affected the office
Health > Network connectivity, drilling into the Sydney location's assessment
Reports > Usage > Microsoft Teams, comparing call and meeting activity by region and device type
Service health > Issue history, filtered to Microsoft Teams and the last 30 days of resolved incidents
why: Network connectivity compiles TCP latency, download speed and UDP quality from the tenant's own clients into an assessment per office location, which is the evidence needed to show a perimeter or ISP problem. Issue history lists Microsoft-side incidents, and the scenario already says none exist. Usage reports describe adoption, not network quality, and Message center announces upcoming changes rather than measuring your network.

q: The Network connectivity page shows a network assessment score of 55 for a regional office. How should the admin interpret it?
opts: Copilot and Teams traffic is blocked at the firewall and the endpoints need to be allow-listed
The office lost connectivity to Microsoft 365 for 45 percent of the last 30 days of operation
Healthy, because any score above 50 shows the Microsoft-owned network is performing correctly for that office
Below the 80 healthy baseline, so investigate the office's network design
why: The score runs from 0 to 100 and averages TCP latency, download speed and UDP quality for the customer's own network, with 80 as the healthy baseline, 60 acceptable and 40 where users might experience issues. A 55 is below acceptable, so the office's design should be investigated. The measurement deliberately excludes Microsoft-owned networks, it is not an availability percentage, and a score does not by itself prove that endpoints are blocked.

q: An admin wants to be emailed when Microsoft posts an incident that affects Exchange Online or SharePoint Online in their tenant, sent to the on-call mailbox as well as their own. What should they configure?
opts: A mail flow rule that forwards Message center posts to the on-call mailbox
A Defender for Office 365 alert policy that emails the on-call mailbox for Exchange anomalies
On the Service health page, Customize > Email, adding both addresses and selecting the two services
A Power Automate flow that polls the Microsoft 365 usage report daily
why: Service health supports email notifications for incidents or advisories for selected services, with up to two addresses per admin. An alert policy responds to security and compliance activities, not Microsoft's service incidents. Mail flow rules act on messages in transit and Message center posts are not mail to be transformed, and a usage report poller would not detect incidents.

q: Contoso's organization theme must show the regional brand to each subsidiary while everyone else keeps the corporate theme. Which two statements about custom themes are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: The default theme applies to everyone who is not assigned a group theme
Up to four additional group themes can be created, each assigned to up to five Microsoft 365 groups
Each subsidiary needs its own tenant, because one tenant supports a single theme
Group themes can only change the color scheme, not the logo
why: A tenant has one default theme plus up to four group themes, and each group theme can be assigned to up to five Microsoft 365 groups; users not matched by a group theme see the default. A single tenant supports several themes, so separate tenants are unnecessary, and each theme has Logos and Colors tabs so logos can differ.

q: An organizer sets Copilot in a Teams meeting to During and after the meeting, but the tenant's transcription policy is Off and nobody else is permitted to transcribe. What happens for licensed participants?
opts: Copilot works for the whole meeting using temporary speech-to-text that is discarded afterward
Copilot runs without transcription for all users because organizer settings override tenant policy
They cannot use Copilot in the meeting, because it needs a transcript that nobody can start
Copilot works only after the meeting, from the recording stored in OneDrive
why: During and after the meeting depends on a transcript, and with the transcription policy Off, licensed users cannot interact with Copilot unless another participant who is allowed to transcribe turns it on. The temporary speech-to-text behavior belongs to the Only during the meeting option. The organizer option does not override the tenant transcription policy, and there is no after-the-meeting mode that works from a recording alone.

q: If a meeting organizer sets Copilot to Off for a Teams meeting, Copilot is unavailable but the meeting can still be recorded and transcribed as usual.
opts: True
False
why: Turning Copilot off for a meeting also turns off recording and transcription for that meeting. An admin can set the default organizer value to Off by policy, but organizers can still change it per meeting.

q: Contoso assigns its 250 Microsoft Copilot licenses to the Sales security group. Most members receive Copilot, but three users in the group still get no Copilot features and their license page shows an error. Which is the most likely cause?
opts: The group has more members than there are available Copilot licenses
Copilot add-on licenses cannot be assigned through groups, only directly to each individual user
The users are missing the Teams license that the Copilot add-on depends on in order to be assigned
Pay-as-you-go billing has not been linked to an Azure subscription
why: Group-based licensing assigns licenses until the subscription runs out and records a 'Not enough licenses' error on the remaining members, which appears on the Errors & issues tab of the license page; buying or freeing licenses and reprocessing fixes it. Group-based licensing does support add-on licenses such as Copilot, Teams is not a prerequisite for the Copilot add-on, and pay-as-you-go billing is a separate model for metered services, not a prerequisite for per-user licenses.

q: Contoso wants SharePoint Advanced Management to reduce stale content before Copilot grounds on it. Which two capabilities address that? (Choose two.) (Choose two.)
opts: Inactive site policies and site attestations that ask owners to confirm a site is still needed
A sensitivity label with encryption on every file in the tenant
A Defender for Office 365 Safe Attachments policy for the sites' libraries
A site ownership policy that notifies when a site has too few owners
why: SAM's content sprawl controls include a site ownership policy, inactive site detection that notifies owners and attestation requests where owners confirm a site's necessity, owners and permissions. Safe Attachments scans files for malware, which is not a lifecycle control, and bulk-encrypting every file is a data protection choice that would not reduce stale content.

q: A finance SharePoint site must only be reachable from compliant devices, even for users who already have permissions. The admin wants to do this at the site level. Which SharePoint Advanced Management capability is intended for it?
opts: Add the finance site to a Restricted SharePoint Search allowed list
Link a Conditional Access policy to the site with an authentication context
Turn on Restricted Content Discovery for the finance site
Apply a retention label to the finance site's document library
why: SAM supports linking a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy to a SharePoint site through an authentication context, so access can require a compliant device for just that site. Restricted Content Discovery and the Restricted SharePoint Search allowed list change search and Copilot visibility, not who can open the site. A retention label governs how long content is kept.

q: A project manager at a partner company only needs to appear in Contoso's address book so staff can email them. They must not sign in or see any Contoso resources. What should be created?
opts: A mail contact
A shared mailbox
A mail user with a Contoso sign-in
A guest user invited through Microsoft Entra B2B
why: A mail contact is an address-book entry for an external address with no sign-in or resource access, which is exactly what is needed. A guest user would be able to authenticate and be given access to groups and sites, a mail user has a directory sign-in account, and a shared mailbox is a mailbox in the tenant used by several people, none of which fit.

q: Contoso's tenant has Microsoft 365 E3 licenses and security defaults enabled. The security team creates a Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for Exchange Online, but the portal will not let them turn the policy on. What should you do first?
opts: Disable security defaults in the Microsoft Entra admin center
Purchase Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses for the tenant
Set the policy to report-only mode instead of on
Exclude the break-glass accounts from the policy
why: Security defaults and Conditional Access are mutually exclusive; while security defaults are on, Conditional Access policies cannot be enabled, so turning security defaults off is the prerequisite. Microsoft 365 E3 already includes Microsoft Entra ID P1, which is all Conditional Access needs; P2 adds risk-based policies and PIM but is not what blocks this. Report-only mode is a good evaluation step, but it does not change the mutual exclusivity, and excluding break-glass accounts is a best practice that comes after the policy can be enabled.

q: Contoso's security policy forbids storing any form of user password credential in the cloud and requires that on-premises account disablement and sign-in hours take effect for cloud sign-ins immediately. Contoso does not want to deploy or maintain an AD FS farm. Which hybrid authentication method should you recommend?
opts: Pass-through authentication
Password hash synchronization with seamless single sign-on
Federation with Active Directory Federation Services
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync with password hash synchronization
why: Pass-through authentication validates each sign-in against on-premises Active Directory through lightweight agents, so no hash is stored in the cloud and on-premises account state, sign-in hours, and password policies are enforced at sign-in time. Password hash synchronization, whether delivered by Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, stores a hash of the password hash in Microsoft Entra ID, which the policy prohibits. Federation would satisfy both requirements but needs the AD FS infrastructure the organization wants to avoid.

q: A Conditional Access policy requires MFA to sign in, and then, for sessions from unmanaged devices, restricts the user to browser-only access with downloads blocked. Which part of the policy is the download-blocking restriction?
opts: A grant control
A sign-in risk condition
A named location condition
A session control
why: Restricting an already-granted session (like blocking downloads via app enforced restrictions) is a session control. Requiring MFA before access is granted at all is the grant control in this scenario, not the download restriction.

q: Several Contoso users clicked links in emails that passed filtering at delivery but were weaponized hours later. You need protection that evaluates the URL at the moment a user clicks it, in email and in Office documents, and that can block the click. Which Defender for Office 365 capability should you configure?
opts: A Safe Links policy
Zero-hour auto purge for phishing messages
A Safe Attachments policy with Dynamic Delivery
An anti-phishing policy with impersonation protection
why: Safe Links rewrites URLs and checks each one against threat intelligence at time of click, in email and in supported Office apps, and can block the click outright. Zero-hour auto purge is the closest alternative, but it retroactively removes delivered messages once they are judged malicious; it does not inspect at the moment of the click and does not cover links inside Office documents. Safe Attachments detonates file attachments, not URLs. Impersonation protection targets lookalike senders and display names, not links that turn malicious after delivery.

q: A Contoso analyst is investigating an attack that began with a phishing email, continued with malware on the recipient's laptop, and ended with anomalous sign-ins from the recipient's account. The analyst wants a single correlated investigation rather than three separate alert queues. Where should the analyst work?
opts: The Incidents queue in the Microsoft Defender portal
Threat Explorer in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
The Risky sign-ins report in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
The device timeline in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
why: Microsoft Defender XDR correlates alerts from Defender for Office 365, Defender for Endpoint, and identity signals into a single incident, so the Incidents queue shows the whole attack chain in one place. Threat Explorer is excellent for the email stage but stops there. The Risky sign-ins report covers only the identity stage, and the device timeline covers only the endpoint stage; each of the three distractors is one of the separate queues the analyst wants to avoid.

q: Contoso creates a DLP policy that blocks external sharing of content containing credit card numbers across Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive. Before enforcing it, the compliance team wants two weeks of data on how many legitimate business activities would match, without users becoming aware of the policy. What should you do first?
opts: Run the policy in simulation mode with policy tips turned off
Run the policy in simulation mode with policy tips turned on
Turn the policy on with the block action set to allow user overrides
Turn the policy on for a pilot group only and review the incident reports
why: Simulation mode records matches and generates reports without taking the configured actions, and leaving policy tips off keeps users unaware, which satisfies both constraints. Simulation with policy tips on still does not block, but it shows tips to users, so they would notice the policy. Allowing overrides still enforces the block for everyone until they override, and a pilot in enforce mode affects real users' work; neither is a measurement-only step.

q: A retention policy set on a SharePoint site says content should be deleted after 3 years. A retention label applied to a specific document in that site says the document must be retained for 7 years. What happens to that document at year 4?
opts: It is deleted, because the site-level retention policy takes precedence
It is deleted at year 3, and a copy is kept in the Preservation Hold library until year 7
It is retained, because the longer retention period and the explicit retain instruction win
It is moved to the site's recycle bin at year 3 and kept there until year 7
why: When retention rules conflict, the longer retention period wins, and an explicit retain instruction generally wins over a delete instruction, so the 7-year retention label preserves the document past year 3. Retention conflicts resolve automatically toward preservation: the document stays in place rather than being deleted, moved to the recycle bin or left waiting for an admin.

q: Contoso has three requirements for its project documents: they must be encrypted and watermarked, they must be deleted automatically five years after creation, and they must be blocked from being shared with guests in Teams. Which three mappings of requirement to Purview capability are correct? (Choose three.)
opts: Encryption and watermark: a sensitivity label
Deletion after five years: a retention label
Blocking sharing with guests: a DLP policy
Watermark: a retention label
Deletion after five years: a sensitivity label
why: Sensitivity labels apply protection to content (encryption, markings such as watermarks, permissions), retention labels govern lifecycle (retain and then delete on a schedule), and DLP policies detect sensitive content and act on sharing, including blocking a share with guests in Teams and SharePoint. A retention label has no marking or protection settings, and a sensitivity label has no deletion schedule; those two near-misses swap the jobs of the two label types.

q: Contoso Legal receives a litigation notice. They must send hold notices to 12 named employees, track who has acknowledged them, and reduce the review volume by removing near-duplicate messages and threading email conversations. All users hold Microsoft 365 E5. Which should you create?
opts: An eDiscovery (Premium) case
An eDiscovery (Standard) case with a hold on the 12 mailboxes
A Content search scoped to the 12 mailboxes with results exported to PST
A Litigation Hold on the 12 mailboxes and a Communication compliance policy
why: Custodian management, hold notifications with acknowledgment tracking, and review-set analytics such as near-duplicate detection and threading are eDiscovery (Premium) features. A Standard case can hold and search the mailboxes, but it has no custodian workflow or analytics. Content search can find and export but cannot hold content or notify custodians. Litigation Hold preserves data, and Communication compliance reviews messages for policy violations; neither notifies custodians or reduces review volume.

q: Nine months ago, an attacker accessed a Contoso executive's mailbox. The executive holds a Microsoft 365 E5 license. Legal needs to know exactly which messages the attacker opened during the compromise. Which capability should you use?
opts: Audit (Premium) search in the Microsoft Purview portal
Audit (Standard) search in the Microsoft Purview portal
Threat Explorer in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Message trace in the Exchange admin center
why: The MailItemsAccessed event that identifies individual items that were read is now generated for Audit (Standard) as well, so the deciding factor is retention: Audit (Premium), which Microsoft 365 E5 includes, keeps records for one year by default and still covers activity from nine months ago. Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default, so nine-month-old activity has already aged out. Threat Explorer shows email threat detections and clicks over a recent window, not mailbox reads. Message trace follows delivery through the transport pipeline and shows nothing about what was opened after delivery.

q: A financial services firm needs to prevent its investment banking team from being able to chat with or find the research team in Teams and SharePoint, to avoid a conflict of interest, while both teams still use the same tenant normally. Which feature enforces this?
opts: Conditional Access policies scoped by group
Information barriers
Sensitivity labels with encryption
Communication compliance policies
why: Information barriers are purpose-built to block communication and collaboration between defined segments of users, exactly the conflict-of-interest scenario described. Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions, not who can communicate with whom, and communication compliance reviews content after the fact rather than blocking contact.

q: An admin wants to grant a user the ability to fully manage DLP policies in Microsoft Purview without granting them any Microsoft Entra directory admin role. How should this be done?
opts: Assign the user to an appropriate Purview compliance role group
Assign the user the Global Administrator role
Assign the user the User Administrator Microsoft Entra role
Enable the Microsoft Purview portal for the tenant so existing admins automatically receive edit rights
why: Purview compliance permissions are managed through role groups, a separate permission layer purpose-built for compliance solutions like DLP, and do not require any Microsoft Entra directory role. Global Administrator or User Administrator would grant far broader access than is needed or requested, and simply enabling the compliance portal doesn't hand out any permissions by itself — role group membership still has to be assigned explicitly.

q: Contoso's CISO wants a single number that tracks the tenant's security posture across identity, devices, apps, and data, with a ranked list of concrete actions (such as enabling MFA for admins) and the points each action would add. Which should you use?
opts: Microsoft Secure Score
Compliance Manager compliance score
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management exposure score
Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk reports
why: Microsoft Secure Score is the posture metric that aggregates identity, device, app, and data recommendations into one score with point-valued improvement actions. Compliance score measures progress against regulatory assessments, not security posture. The exposure score is limited to device vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. ID Protection reports show detected risky users and sign-ins; they do not score configuration or recommend improvements across workloads.

q: An organization is preparing for an ISO 27001 audit and wants to track which required controls Microsoft already fulfills as the cloud provider versus which controls the organization itself must implement and attest to. Which tool is designed for this?
opts: Microsoft Secure Score
Defender for Cloud Apps
Compliance Manager
Insider Risk Management
why: Compliance Manager translates regulatory requirements into improvement actions and explicitly distinguishes Microsoft-managed actions from customer-responsibility actions, matching the shared-responsibility tracking described. Secure Score measures general security posture rather than mapping to specific regulatory frameworks.

q: After Contoso disables security defaults to adopt Conditional Access, legacy authentication protocols remain blocked for all users until an administrator explicitly re-enables them.
opts: True
False
why: The legacy authentication block is one of the protections security defaults provides; turning security defaults off removes it along with the rest of the baseline. An organization moving to Conditional Access must recreate that protection as a policy that blocks legacy authentication clients, which is why the switch should be planned with report-only testing rather than assumed to carry over.

q: Contoso uses pass-through authentication as its sign-in method. Enabling password hash synchronization alongside it allows Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials for Contoso users.
opts: True
False
why: Leaked-credential detection compares synchronized password hashes against credential dumps, so it requires password hash synchronization even when PTA handles the actual sign-in. Running PHS in parallel also provides a fallback if the PTA agents become unavailable. The misconception is that choosing PTA rules PHS out, or that ID Protection can evaluate credentials it never receives.

q: When a user deletes a OneDrive file that carries a standard seven-year retention label, the file disappears from the user's view but a copy is kept in the Preservation Hold library until the retention period ends.
opts: True
False
why: A standard (non-record) retention label does not block deletion; it guarantees the content survives it. The deleted file moves to the site's Preservation Hold library, where it stays searchable by eDiscovery until the period expires. Only record and regulatory-record labels actually prevent the user from deleting the item, which is the distinction this statement tests.

q: Communication compliance automatically blocks a flagged message from being sent, similar to a DLP policy in block mode.
opts: True
False
why: Communication compliance is a detect-and-review workflow that routes flagged communications to reviewers after the fact; it does not block a message from sending the way a DLP policy configured to block can.

q: Insider Risk Management reveals a flagged user's full identity to every reviewer immediately when a case is created.
opts: True
False
why: Insider Risk Management pseudonymizes user identities in case alerts by default, until an investigator explicitly needs to reveal them, to balance risk detection against employee privacy during review.

q: In a tenant where some users hold Audit (Premium) and others hold only Audit (Standard), audit records generated by an Audit (Standard) user are kept for 180 days by default, regardless of the other users' licenses.
opts: True
False
why: Audit retention is applied per user based on that user's own license: Premium-licensed users' records default to one year, while Standard-licensed users' records default to 180 days unless an audit log retention policy extends them. One investigator holding Premium does not lengthen retention for the people being investigated.

q: An information barriers policy that blocks the Investment Banking and Research segments from communicating also blocks email between members of the two segments in Exchange Online.
opts: True
False
why: Information barriers enforce restrictions in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive: chats, calls, meetings, file sharing, and people search between segments. They do not apply to Exchange Online email; blocking email between groups requires a mail flow (transport) rule. The misconception is assuming one segmentation policy covers every workload.

q: Contoso's Conditional Access policy for SharePoint Online on unmanaged devices must require MFA, limit users to browser-only access with downloads blocked, and force re-authentication every four hours. Which two of these requirements are implemented as session controls? (Choose two.)
opts: Browser-only access with downloads blocked, using app enforced restrictions
Re-authentication every four hours, using sign-in frequency
Requiring MFA before access is allowed
Requiring a compliant device before access is allowed
why: App enforced restrictions and sign-in frequency both shape an already-granted session, so they are configured under the policy's Session controls. Requiring MFA is a grant control, since it decides whether access is permitted at all. Requiring a compliant device is also a grant control, and it is not even part of this scenario's requirements; it is included as a near-miss for candidates who associate 'device' with session behavior.

q: Contoso applies a retention policy to all SharePoint sites that retains content for three years and then deletes it. HR applies a retention label that retains for seven years to certain files on the HR site. In year two, an HR user deletes one of those labeled files. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A copy of the deleted file is preserved in the Preservation Hold library until the seven-year period ends
The site policy's three-year deletion does not remove the labeled file, because the longer retention period wins
The user is prevented from deleting the labeled file while the retention period is in effect
The labeled file is permanently deleted at year three, because the site policy was applied first
why: A standard retention label lets the user delete the file from view, but retention preserves a copy in the Preservation Hold library for the remainder of the seven years. When a policy and a label conflict, the longer retention period and the explicit retain instruction win, so the three-year deletion does not apply to labeled files. Deletion is only blocked when an item is declared a record, and which rule was applied first plays no part in the precedence.

q: Eight months ago an attacker compromised a Contoso mailbox. Investigators now need the list of individual messages the attacker read. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: If the mailbox owner was licensed only for Audit (Standard), records from eight months ago have already aged out of the 180-day default retention
If the mailbox owner was licensed for Audit (Premium), the default one-year retention still covers the activity
Assigning an Audit (Premium) license to the user now restores the audit records that already expired
A historical message trace can substitute for the audit records, because it shows which messages were opened
why: Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default, so eight-month-old activity is gone, whereas Audit (Premium) retains records for a year by default. The mailbox-access event this investigation depends on (MailItemsAccessed) is now generated for Audit (Standard) too, so retention is what separates the two. Licensing cannot retroactively recreate records that have expired or were never generated. Message trace reports delivery through the transport pipeline over a limited window; it never records which items a signed-in user opened.

q: Contoso configures an Insider Risk Management policy for data theft by departing users and connects the Microsoft 365 HR connector. Which two statements about the resulting alerts are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: Alerts display pseudonymized user names until a user with the appropriate role reveals the identity
Resignation and termination dates imported through the HR connector act as triggering events for the policy
The policy blocks the flagged downloads in real time once an alert reaches high severity
Alerts for the policy are generated only after the user's termination date has passed
why: Insider Risk Management pseudonymizes identities in alerts by default, and the HR connector supplies the departure dates that trigger scoring for the departing-user policy template. The policy itself detects and scores activity for investigation; it does not block downloads, which would be DLP's job (or adaptive protection feeding a DLP policy). The policy watches a window of activity before and after the departure date, since the risky behavior usually happens before the last day.

q: An admin wants a sensitivity label that, when applied to a Microsoft 365 Team, automatically makes the team private and blocks access from unmanaged devices, rather than encrypting any individual file. Which sensitivity label scope must be enabled for this label?
opts: Files & emails scope only
Groups & sites scope
Schematized data assets scope
Meetings and calendar events scope
why: The Groups & sites scope applies container-level settings — privacy, external access, and unmanaged device restrictions — to the Microsoft 365 Group or Team itself. The Files & emails scope only protects individual documents and messages (meetings are part of that same items scope, not a separate one), and the Schematized data assets scope covers database columns and similar assets in the Purview Data Map; none of those touch a team's container-level settings.

q: Two DLP policies both match the same document, but their configured actions conflict. What determines which policy's action actually takes effect on that document?
opts: The policy with the numerically larger priority number is evaluated first and applies its action
The policy with higher priority (a lower priority number, evaluated first) applies its matching rule's action
Both actions are applied simultaneously regardless of the conflict
Whichever policy was created most recently overrides any older, conflicting policy
why: DLP policies are evaluated in priority order, where a lower priority number is evaluated first and effectively wins when policies conflict; rules within a policy are then evaluated top-down. Creation date and a numerically higher priority number do not determine precedence — the priority ranking does.

q: Contoso enforces risk-based Conditional Access policies. A user's sign-in is flagged with high sign-in risk because of impossible travel, and the same account separately shows high user risk from a leaked-credential detection. The user completes MFA successfully for the risky sign-in. What is the account's state afterward?
opts: The sign-in risk is remediated, but the user risk remains until a secure password change
Both the sign-in risk and the user risk are remediated by the successful MFA
Neither risk is remediated until an administrator dismisses the user risk
The user risk is remediated, but the sign-in risk remains until an administrator confirms it safe
why: Sign-in risk is a per-session signal, so satisfying MFA remediates that sign-in. User risk from leaked credentials indicates the password itself is compromised, and it is remediated by a secure password change (self-service through a user-risk policy, or an admin reset); MFA alone does not clear it. Admin dismissal is a manual option, not a requirement, and the claim that user risk clears while sign-in risk lingers reverses which risk each remediation addresses.

q: A retention policy needs to automatically apply to every user in the Finance department, and stay current as employees move into or out of Finance, without an admin manually updating a list of names. Which Microsoft Purview scoping feature should be used?
opts: A static scope that lists each Finance user by name
An adaptive scope based on a department attribute query
A sensitivity label auto-labeling policy
A retention label published to the Finance users
why: Adaptive scopes dynamically include users, groups, or sites based on attribute queries like department, so the policy's coverage recalculates automatically as attributes or membership change. A static scope would require manual updates every time someone joins or leaves Finance, defeating the requirement. Sensitivity auto-labeling applies protection, not retention, and publishing a retention label only makes it available for users to apply by hand; it does not scope or apply a policy automatically.

q: A Contoso compliance analyst must search the unified audit log for a quarterly review and must not be able to change audit retention policies or any other Purview configuration. The analyst currently holds no roles. You need to follow least privilege. What should you do?
opts: Add the analyst to the Audit Reader role group in Microsoft Purview
Add the analyst to the Audit Manager role group in Microsoft Purview
Add the analyst to the Compliance Administrator role group in Microsoft Purview
Assign the analyst the Reports Reader Microsoft Entra role
why: Audit Reader grants exactly the View-Only Audit Logs permission needed to search the unified audit log. Audit Manager is the near-miss: it also allows creating and managing audit log retention policies, which the scenario forbids. Compliance Administrator spans most Purview solutions and is far broader than needed. Reports Reader is a Microsoft Entra role for usage reports and does not include audit log search.

q: In Privileged Identity Management, a user with an active Global Administrator assignment that expires in one month holds the role continuously for that month without activating it, unlike a user with an eligible assignment.
opts: True
False
why: A time-bound active assignment is standing access for its whole window: the role is always on with no activation, justification, approval, or per-use audit entry. An eligible assignment grants nothing until the user activates it, typically with MFA, a justification, and optionally an approver, for a limited activation duration. Both have an end date, but only eligibility delivers just-in-time access.

q: Contoso adds the ISO 27001 and GDPR assessments to Compliance Manager, then enables MFA for all administrators. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: The MFA improvement action can contribute points to both assessments at the same time
Actions Microsoft is responsible for appear in each assessment with Microsoft's own test status, without Contoso implementing them
Marking the MFA action as implemented causes Compliance Manager to configure the Conditional Access policy
A 100 percent compliance score means Contoso has achieved ISO 27001 certification
why: Improvement actions are shared across assessments, so one control such as admin MFA earns credit wherever a template requires it, and Microsoft-managed actions are tracked with Microsoft's attestation under the shared responsibility model. Compliance Manager tracks and scores; it never configures tenant settings itself. The compliance score is an internal progress measure, not an auditor's certification.

q: Contoso requires MFA through Conditional Access. Most users registered SMS as their only method. You need to move users to Microsoft Authenticator with number matching and stop new SMS registrations, without immediately locking out users who have only SMS today. What should you do first?
opts: Configure a registration campaign for Microsoft Authenticator in the Authentication methods policy
Apply the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength in the Conditional Access policy
Disable the SMS method in the Authentication methods policy
Enable per-user MFA enforcement for all users in the legacy MFA portal
why: A registration campaign prompts users who still rely on weaker methods to set up Microsoft Authenticator at sign-in, with a snooze window, so adoption rises before SMS is switched off; that is the right first move. Requiring phishing-resistant strength would immediately reject SMS sign-ins and also reject Authenticator push, which is not phishing-resistant. Disabling SMS now locks out everyone who has nothing else registered. Per-user MFA is the legacy mechanism Microsoft steers customers away from, and it does not drive Authenticator registration.

q: Contoso wants any document saved to SharePoint that contains credit card numbers to be encrypted automatically, with no action by the user who saved it. Users should keep working on the files normally. Which should you configure?
opts: A sensitivity label auto-labeling policy for SharePoint with a label that applies encryption
A DLP policy for SharePoint with an action that encrypts matching content
A mandatory labeling policy that sets a default encrypted label for all documents
An auto-apply retention label policy that targets the credit card sensitive information type
why: Service-side auto-labeling scans content in SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange and applies a sensitivity label, including one that encrypts, with no user involvement. The DLP encrypt action is the near-miss: it exists, but it applies only to Exchange email, so it cannot encrypt SharePoint files. A mandatory default label depends on users saving from a client that applies it and would encrypt every document, not just those containing card numbers. A retention label governs how long content is kept and cannot encrypt anything.

q: An organization wants to detect when an employee who is about to resign downloads an unusually large volume of files shortly before their last day, correlated with their HR-flagged departure status. Separately, they want to review whether employees are sharing offensive language in Teams chats company-wide. Which two Purview solutions address these, respectively?
opts: Insider Risk Management for the departure scenario, and Communication compliance for the language review
Communication compliance for the departure scenario, and Insider Risk Management for the language review
eDiscovery (Premium) handles both, since its analytics can also flag risky behavior and offensive language
DSPM for AI handles both, since it monitors unusual data access patterns and risky messages
why: Insider Risk Management correlates HR signals like departure status with activity like unusual downloads to flag potential data exfiltration. Communication compliance reviews message content for policy violations like offensive language. Swapping the two assigns each tool the job it does not do, eDiscovery is a search/hold tool rather than a behavioral risk detector, and DSPM for AI is scoped to AI interaction risk, not general file-download or chat-content review.

q: A tenant currently relies on Security Defaults for baseline protection. The security team wants a more advanced rule — block sign-in from a specific country except for two named traveling executives — while keeping simple baseline MFA enforced everywhere else with no ongoing manual policy upkeep for every new user. What should they do?
opts: Turn off Security Defaults and rebuild its baseline protections, plus the country-based block, as Conditional Access policies
Keep Security Defaults enabled and add a separate Conditional Access policy for the country-based block exception
Leave Security Defaults enabled, since it already supports per-country, per-user exceptions natively
Keep Security Defaults enabled and add the two executives to an exclusion list within Security Defaults
why: Security Defaults and custom Conditional Access policies can't run side by side — enabling the granular, per-country exception this scenario needs requires turning off Security Defaults and rebuilding its baseline protections (like tenant-wide MFA) as explicit Conditional Access policies. Security Defaults itself is an all-or-nothing baseline with no per-country logic and no exclusion list of any kind, so neither 'keep it and add an exception' option is possible.

q: A university wants students to self-request access to a bundled set of resources — a Team, a SharePoint site, and a licensed app — through a catalog, with a manager approval step and automatic expiration at the end of the semester, instead of an admin manually granting each resource. Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance feature fits?
opts: Access reviews that recertify existing access
Entitlement management (access packages)
Privileged Identity Management with eligible roles
Conditional Access policies for the Team and app
why: Entitlement management bundles resources into an access package that users can request through a self-service catalog, with approval workflows and automatic expiration built in, exactly matching this scenario. Access reviews recertify access that already exists rather than provisioning it, PIM governs role eligibility, and Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions, not resource bundling.

q: A user tries to install a third-party app that requests permission to read every mailbox in the tenant through Microsoft Graph. The organization wants this kind of high-privilege request to always be reviewed and approved by an administrator rather than left to the individual user. What should be configured?
opts: A Conditional Access policy blocking that specific app
An app consent policy requiring admin consent for that permission level
Disabling Microsoft Graph access for the entire tenant
An information barrier between the user and the app
why: App consent policies control whether a user can grant consent themselves or whether a request must route to an admin through the admin consent workflow, which directly matches the requirement. Blocking one app with Conditional Access doesn't govern consent for every similar app going forward, disabling Graph tenant-wide would break legitimate integrations, and information barriers govern user-to-user communication, not app permission consent.

q: A broker-dealer must guarantee regulators that a 7-year retention policy on trade communications cannot be shortened or disabled by anyone, including its own Global Administrators, once it is finalized. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this guarantee?
opts: Preservation Lock on the retention policy
A litigation hold placed on each mailbox individually
Customer Lockbox
Information barriers
why: Preservation Lock prevents anyone, including a Global Administrator, from turning off, deleting or shortening a locked retention policy (it can only be extended), matching this exact regulatory requirement. A per-mailbox litigation hold doesn't lock the policy itself against admin changes, Customer Lockbox governs Microsoft support engineer access, and information barriers govern communication between user groups.

q: A bank wants to require that administrators sign in using only phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as a FIDO2 security key or certificate-based authentication, rather than accepting any MFA method including SMS. Which Conditional Access control should be configured?
opts: A session control that limits sign-in frequency for administrators
A grant control that requires a phishing-resistant authentication strength
A grant control that requires multifactor authentication by any method
Security defaults, which enforce MFA for all administrator roles
why: Authentication strength is a grant control that can mandate a specific combination of methods, like phishing-resistant ones, rather than accepting any second factor equally. A plain 'require MFA' control accepts weaker methods like SMS too, a session control only restricts an already-granted session rather than which method was used, and security defaults cannot be customized to this degree.

q: If a security group that is assigned the Exchange Administrator role is onboarded to PIM for Groups, making a user's membership eligible means the user holds Exchange Administrator only while an activated membership is in effect.
opts: True
False
why: PIM for Groups makes group membership itself just-in-time. Any Microsoft Entra role, app role, or license the group grants is effective only while the user's activated membership lasts, so the role becomes just-in-time without configuring PIM separately on the role. The near-miss is assuming the role assignment to the group bypasses the membership activation.

q: A university creates an access package in entitlement management that bundles a Team, a SharePoint site, and an app role for a semester course. Which two statements about this access package are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: The request policy can be set so that access expires on a fixed date at the end of the semester
The request policy can require the requestor's manager to approve before access is granted
A recurring access review must be configured on the package before it can be published
Students from a partner university cannot request the package, because access packages are internal-only
why: Access package policies support lifecycle settings that expire access on a date or after a number of days, and approval stages that can name the requestor's manager as approver. Access reviews on a package are optional, not a publishing prerequisite. External users can be allowed to request packages through connected organizations, which is one of entitlement management's main uses for guest onboarding.

q: An employee is terminated and their Microsoft Entra account is immediately disabled. Minutes later, that employee's laptop — still holding a previously issued access token — attempts to open a SharePoint file. With Continuous Access Evaluation enabled, what happens?
opts: Access is revoked almost immediately, since CAE evaluates the critical account-disabled event in near real time
Access continues working normally until the token's originally scheduled expiration time arrives
Access is revoked, but only once the next scheduled access review cycle happens to run
Access continues working until an admin separately issues a remote wipe of the laptop
why: Continuous Access Evaluation re-evaluates a token near real time when a critical event like account disablement occurs, revoking access in roughly minutes rather than waiting out the token's full remaining lifetime. Without CAE, the token could otherwise keep working until it expires on its own schedule, and this has nothing to do with a periodic access review cycle or a separate remote wipe action.

q: A document has been declared a regulatory record under Microsoft Purview Records Management. An admin later tries to remove its retention label to free up the document for editing. What happens?
opts: The removal fails; neither the label nor the record's key properties can be changed before the retention period ends
The admin can remove the label right away, since admin accounts are exempt from records management locks
The label is removed, though the document's underlying content stays unchanged and still editable
The record is deleted automatically the instant anyone, including an admin, attempts to remove its label
why: Declaring an item a regulatory record locks down both its label and key properties so that nobody, including an admin, can change or remove them until the retention period actually ends — a stronger guarantee than a standard retention label allows. Admin accounts are not exempt, no removal succeeds at all in this scenario, and no deletion is triggered by a blocked removal attempt.

q: An Exact Data Match (EDM) sensitive information type flags any text that merely resembles a pattern, like digits shaped like a credit card number, regardless of whether that exact value is real.
opts: True
False
why: This describes a standard pattern-based sensitive information type, not EDM. An EDM sensitive information type instead checks content against an actual uploaded dataset of real values, catching only true matches and sharply reducing pattern-based false positives.

q: Contoso publishes three retention labels in SharePoint: a standard label, a label that marks items as records, and a label that marks items as regulatory records. Which two statements about labeled documents are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: A regulatory record's label cannot be removed by anyone, including a Global Administrator, before the retention period ends
A document labeled as a record can be temporarily unlocked by an authorized user in SharePoint to edit its content
A document with the standard label cannot be deleted by any user, including its owner, until the retention period ends
A document labeled as a regulatory record can be unlocked for editing by an authorized user in the same way as a record
why: Regulatory records are the most restrictive: the label cannot be removed or changed by anyone, and the content cannot be edited or unlocked. Records allow an authorized user to toggle the record lock in SharePoint to make edits, then re-lock the item. A standard retention label never blocks deletion; it preserves a copy in the Preservation Hold library instead, so the claim that a standard label blocks deletion describes record behavior, not standard-label behavior.

q: Contoso's brand name and its headquarters city keep appearing in weak user passwords like 'Fabrikam!City1'. Which action blocks those variants with the least effort?
opts: Enable security defaults, which blocks every password that contains a company name
Disable the global banned password list so that only the organization's own list is applied
Add the base terms Fabrikam and the city name to the custom banned password list
List every variation that users have tried in the custom banned password list one by one
why: The custom banned password list takes up to 1,000 base terms and the validation algorithm normalizes and fuzzy-matches variants, so listing the base terms catches the combinations. Enumerating variations wastes the limited list, the global list cannot be disabled and would not be a good idea anyway, and security defaults enforce MFA and related protections but have no company-name blocking.

q: Contoso extends Microsoft Entra Password Protection to its on-premises Active Directory. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: A Password Protection proxy service on a domain-joined server relays policy requests, so domain controllers never contact the internet directly
The DC agent must be installed on every domain controller for consistent enforcement
An AD DS schema extension must be run before installing the DC agent
Password hash synchronization to Entra ID is required for the feature to work
why: The policy is only enforced on domain controllers that run the DC agent, so every DC needs it, and the proxy forwards policy downloads from Entra ID so DCs do not need internet access. The feature does not depend on password hash sync and requires no schema change, since it uses existing containers and service connection point objects.

q: Contoso is still allowing SMS and voice methods through the old per-tenant multifactor authentication settings page, and wants phishing-resistant methods enabled only for the security team. Which is the supported place to do this?
opts: Per-user MFA status, setting the security team to Enforced
The legacy multifactor authentication settings page, adding the security group to the allowed methods
The legacy self-service password reset authentication methods list
The Authentication methods policy, enabling FIDO2 or passkeys for the security group
why: The Authentication methods policy is the recommended place to enable methods for specific groups, and the legacy MFA and SSPR method settings could no longer manage authentication methods after September 30, 2025.
