The legacy pages apply to all users with no group targeting, and per-user MFA status enforces MFA but does not choose which methods are available.

q: A user whose password is synchronized from on-premises Active Directory tries self-service password reset and is told to contact an administrator, although SSPR is enabled for them and they registered two methods. What is missing?
opts: Password writeback
A custom banned password list
A Temporary Access Pass issued to the user by an administrator
Membership in a Microsoft Entra administrative unit for the user's office
why: When the password is mastered on-premises, SSPR can proceed only if password writeback is configured; without it the user is directed to the administrator. A Temporary Access Pass is for passwordless onboarding, administrative units scope admin permissions, and the custom banned list only affects what passwords are accepted.

q: Contoso must stop guests from being invited from consumer email domains and let only members and a Guest Inviter group invite others. Where is this configured?
opts: Teams admin center external access, using a blocked domain list for federation
SharePoint admin center external sharing, set to Existing guests only for the whole tenant
A Conditional Access policy that blocks guest users from all cloud apps
Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings
why: External collaboration settings control who can invite guests and which domains are allowed or denied for B2B collaboration. SharePoint sharing and Teams external access are separate layers that affect those workloads only, and a Conditional Access block would let the invitation happen but stop guests from using apps rather than controlling who can be invited.

q: Contoso trusts its partner Fabrikam and wants Fabrikam's guests who already completed MFA in their home tenant to avoid a second MFA prompt when opening Contoso resources. What should be configured?
opts: Cross-tenant access settings that trust Fabrikam's MFA claims
A named location for Fabrikam's IP ranges that is excluded from all Conditional Access policies
A Conditional Access session control that sets sign-in frequency to never
Security defaults disabled for the entire Contoso tenant
why: Inbound trust settings in cross-tenant access let Contoso accept MFA (and device compliance) claims from a specific partner tenant, so the guest satisfies the MFA requirement once. Excluding IP ranges weakens protection for any user on those ranges, disabling security defaults affects everyone, and sign-in frequency settings do not accept a partner's MFA claim.

q: HR gives IT a CSV of 600 new hires and asks that each be created with the right department and a group membership before day one. Which approach is most appropriate for repeatable bulk creation?
opts: Invite all 600 as guests now and promote them to members once they have started
Run Import-Csv with New-MgUser after connecting with User.ReadWrite.All
Create each user in the admin center one at a time, then copy the settings from the first one
Use the MSOnline module's New-MsolUser cmdlet in a loop over the CSV rows
why: Microsoft Graph PowerShell with Import-Csv and New-MgUser handles repeatable bulk creation, and the delegated scope User.ReadWrite.All is what the cmdlet needs. Hand-creating 600 users is slow and inconsistent, the MSOnline module is retired, and guests are external identities that would need conversion rather than new employees.

q: Contoso wants strong email protection for all staff without tuning individual settings, with the highest sensitivity for executives, who are phishing targets. What should the admin do?
opts: Disable preset policies and edit the default policies for each workload
Rely on Built-in protection alone, because it already covers every Defender feature for all users
Standard preset for all recipients and Strict preset for the executive group
Create custom anti-phishing, Safe Links and Safe Attachments policies for each individual user
why: Preset policies apply Microsoft's recommended settings with minimal tuning: Standard for the general population and Strict for high-risk users such as executives, and the Strict assignment takes precedence for those users. Per-user custom policies are exactly the tuning effort the requirement avoids, Built-in protection only gives baseline Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and editing defaults gives up the managed recommended settings.

q: Built-in protection in the preset security policies applies only to users who are not covered by the Standard policy, the Strict policy or a custom Safe Links or Safe Attachments policy.
opts: True
False
why: Built-in protection supplies baseline Safe Links and Safe Attachments coverage to users who are not excluded from it and are not included in Standard, Strict or a custom policy for those features, so it acts as the floor rather than an addition on top.

q: A user reports a suspicious email, and Contoso wants Defender for Office 365 to gather evidence and recommend remediation, such as soft-deleting similar messages, for a security operator to approve. Which capability does this?
opts: Attack simulation training campaigns that assign training modules to users
Automated investigation and response (AIR) in Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, with a pending-action approval
Priority account tagging that marks executives so they get extra visibility in reports
Safe Links time-of-click protection, which rewrites URLs and checks them when a user clicks
why: AIR starts automated investigations from alerts such as user-reported phish and proposes remediation actions that an approver accepts or rejects, and it is part of Plan 2. Safe Links checks URLs at click time and does not investigate, attack simulation trains users, and priority account tagging changes visibility for selected users.

q: The security team wants to measure and improve how well staff recognize phishing. Which two actions use attack simulation training? (Choose two.)
opts: Block external senders with an anti-spam policy
Launch a credential harvest simulation to a target group
Create a Safe Attachments policy that detonates attachments
Assign a training campaign to users who clicked the simulated link
why: Attack simulation training lets admins send simulated phishing using techniques like credential harvest and assign training, including to users who fail the simulation. Safe Attachments and anti-spam are protective filters that act on real mail and do not train or measure users.

q: A security admin sees a DLP alert in the Microsoft Defender portal that is part of a larger incident. What advantage does this integration provide?
opts: Related alerts from email, endpoint and identity are correlated into one incident for triage
The matched sensitive content is copied into the incident for external sharing
The alert is deleted from Microsoft Purview after the incident is closed
The DLP policy automatically switches from simulation to enforce mode
why: Defender XDR correlates alerts from several workloads into incidents so investigations follow one story. Alert correlation does not change a policy's mode, delete the alert in Purview, or copy content out for sharing.

q: Compliance asks for a single view that shows where sensitive data lives across Microsoft 365, Azure and third-party sources, prioritized by objectives such as preventing oversharing, with Copilot-related risk included. Which is the current Purview solution?
opts: Data Security Posture Management for AI (classic), which only reports on AI activity
Compliance Manager, which scores controls against regulatory templates
Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
Content explorer, which lists items that carry a sensitivity label
why: The current DSPM experience covers Microsoft 365, Azure, Fabric and third-party platforms and guides work through data security objectives, including AI observability. The classic DSPM for AI view receives no new features and is limited to AI activity, Content explorer lists labeled items without objective-driven workflows, and Compliance Manager scores regulatory controls.

q: Contoso uses DSPM for AI (classic) before the Copilot pilot. Which two outcomes can it expect? (Choose two.)
opts: One-click recommended policies that can be turned on for AI activity
A weekly data risk assessment of the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage
Automatic removal of every overshared permission it finds
Immediate data in reports as soon as a policy is created
why: DSPM for AI (classic) automatically assesses the top 100 SharePoint sites weekly for oversharing and offers recommended policies that can be activated in one click. It reports risk but does not remediate permissions itself, and newly created policies need time (allow at least 24 hours) before data appears.

q: Contoso purchased 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, which remain unassigned in the subscription. Managers with Microsoft 365 E3 report that Copilot is unavailable in Word and Outlook, although Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat works for them. What should you do?
opts: Assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot license to the managers, for example through a security group
Turn on Copilot for Word and Outlook on the Copilot settings page in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Upgrade the managers from Microsoft 365 E3 to Microsoft 365 E5
Enable web content grounding for the tenant so Copilot can start responding in the apps
why: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on that must be assigned to each user on top of an eligible base license; licenses sitting unassigned in the subscription do nothing, and the free Copilot Chat working is exactly the symptom of an eligible user without the add-on. The admin center Copilot settings page controls behavior for licensed users, not entitlement. Microsoft 365 E5 does not include Copilot either, and web grounding only affects whether responses can use public web content.

q: A licensed Contoso user asks Copilot what the team decided about Project Falcon. Copilot synthesizes an answer from a Teams chat, two emails, and a document, none of which contains that exact phrase, and cites only items the user already has access to. Which component makes this possible?
opts: The Semantic Index for Copilot
A Copilot connector
Microsoft Search keyword indexing alone
The Copilot Studio orchestrator
why: The Semantic Index builds an encrypted, Graph-based map of content and relationships across a user's mail, chats, and files, so Copilot can reason about meaning rather than matching keywords, while staying permission-trimmed to what the user can already open. A Copilot connector (formerly a Graph connector) brings external, non-Microsoft 365 content into that index; it is not what grounds native content. Keyword indexing alone would miss items that lack the phrase, and the Copilot Studio orchestrator drives custom agents, not Microsoft 365 Copilot's grounding.

q: A file has been shared tenant-wide with an "Anyone in the organization" link for years, and almost no one who has that access actually needs it. A user with that broad access asks Copilot to summarize the file and Copilot does so. What is the most accurate explanation of what happened?
opts: Copilot silently granted the user new access to the file that they did not previously have
This isn't possible — Copilot refuses to summarize any file that has ever had a tenant-wide sharing link
Copilot surfaced content the user already had permission to see, exposing an oversharing risk that already existed
Copilot bypassed SharePoint's permission model entirely because it authenticates using its own separate identity
why: Copilot only surfaces content the requesting user already has permission to view, so this behavior reflects pre-existing oversharing rather than any new access Copilot created. It is exactly why oversharing review matters before a broad Copilot rollout.

q: While a full SharePoint permissions review is underway, an admin wants a fast way to keep a set of legacy sites out of both organization-wide search and Copilot summarization, without changing any user's existing site permissions yet. What should they use?
opts: Restricted Content Discovery in SharePoint Advanced Management
Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management
A sensitivity label with the Groups & sites scope that sets the sites to private
A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location
why: Restricted Content Discovery keeps the selected sites out of organization-wide search and Copilot responses while leaving every permission untouched, which is the only option that satisfies the 'no permission changes yet' constraint (it is the successor to Restricted SharePoint Search, whose new enablement is blocked from July 31, 2026). Restricted access control and a private-site label both change who can access the sites, which is the disruptive step the team is deferring. A Copilot DLP policy acts on sensitive content in Copilot interactions; it does not hide whole sites from search.

q: Contoso already runs DLP and sensitivity labeling. The CISO asks for a view of which generative AI sites and apps employees paste sensitive data into, including non-Microsoft AI sites, along with recommended Purview policies to reduce that risk, with minimal setup. Which should you use?
opts: Data Security Posture Management for AI in Microsoft Purview
Cloud app discovery in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Insider Risk Management browsing indicators
Activity explorer in Microsoft Purview
why: DSPM for AI is built for this: it reports on sensitive information in prompts to Copilot and third-party AI sites and offers one-click recommended policies such as DLP for pasting into AI sites. Cloud app discovery shows which AI apps are in use and their risk scores, but not what sensitive data was entered or which Purview policies to deploy. Insider Risk Management scores individual users' behavior rather than giving a tenant-wide data view. Activity explorer shows activity on labeled and classified content, not a dedicated AI usage posture.

q: Contoso's 'Highly Confidential' sensitivity label applies markings but no encryption, and Legal does not want to change how the labeled files open. Users who can open those files must not be able to have Microsoft 365 Copilot summarize or quote their content. The files are spread across many sites. What should you configure?
opts: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location and a condition on the sensitivity label
Encryption on the sensitivity label that grants users View but not Extract rights
Restricted SharePoint Search covering the sites that hold labeled files
A retention label with a short deletion schedule applied to the labeled files
why: A DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can stop Copilot from processing content that carries the label, leaving file access and the label itself unchanged. Removing the Extract right through label encryption also keeps Copilot from using the content, but it changes the label to encrypt files, which Legal ruled out. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) works at the site level, would hide unlabeled content too, and has no effect on files recently opened by or shared directly with the user. A retention label governs deletion, not Copilot behavior.

q: A department wants a lightweight agent that answers questions using only the content of one specific SharePoint site, inheriting that site's existing permissions, built with minimal effort. What is the fastest supported way to create this?
opts: Create an agent directly from the SharePoint site
Build a declarative agent in Copilot Studio and add the site as a knowledge source
Deploy a Copilot connector for the site before building an agent
Build a custom engine agent that calls the SharePoint REST API
why: Creating an agent from the SharePoint site itself takes a few clicks, grounds the agent in that site's content, and inherits the site's permissions automatically, which is the fastest supported path. A declarative agent in Copilot Studio with the site as a knowledge source also works and respects permissions, but it is more setup than the scenario needs. SharePoint content is already indexed in Microsoft Graph, so a Copilot connector adds nothing, and a custom engine agent is the most effort of all.

q: Contoso's security team wants the Copilot Studio agents built by business units to be visible in Microsoft Entra as first-class identities, so they can be inventoried, included in access reviews, and governed with the same lifecycle tools used for service principals. Which capability provides this?
opts: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
A manually created app registration and service principal for each agent
Microsoft Entra workload identity federation
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management
why: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives agents their own identity objects in Microsoft Entra so they appear in the directory and can be governed like other identities. Creating an app registration per agent is the manual near-miss: it is laborious and depends on each business unit remembering to do it. Workload identity federation lets external workloads such as pipelines obtain tokens without secrets, and Permissions Management is a multicloud entitlement (CIEM) tool; neither represents agents in the directory.

q: Contoso's six SOC analysts want a generative AI assistant inside the Microsoft Defender portal to summarize incidents and write KQL hunting queries. Procurement will not buy per-user AI licenses for the whole company. What should you purchase?
opts: Security Compute Units for Microsoft Security Copilot
Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses for the six analysts
Copilot Studio capacity packs
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps licenses for the analysts
why: Microsoft Security Copilot is the security-specific assistant embedded in Defender, Entra, Purview, and Intune, and it is purchased as provisioned Security Compute Units rather than per user, so six analysts can share capacity. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the productivity assistant for Office apps and does not provide the Defender experience. Copilot Studio capacity funds custom agents, and Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB with no AI assistant of its own.

q: An organization wants Copilot to be able to ground answers in content from a third-party wiki that lives outside Microsoft 365, while still respecting that wiki's own access control list. What should be configured?
opts: A Copilot connector for the wiki, with its permissions mapped to the wiki's access control list
A Copilot Studio agent that uses the wiki as a knowledge source through a connector
A nightly export of the wiki into a SharePoint site readable by everyone in the organization
Restricted SharePoint Search with the wiki added to the allowed list
why: A Copilot connector (formerly a Graph connector) indexes the wiki into Microsoft Graph and the Semantic Index so Microsoft 365 Copilot can ground on it, and mapping the connector's ACL to the source is what keeps results permission-trimmed. A Copilot Studio agent with the wiki as a knowledge source would let that one agent answer wiki questions, but it does not make the content available to Microsoft 365 Copilot generally. A nightly export readable by everyone discards the wiki's access control list, creating oversharing. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) only governs SharePoint sites and cannot include an external system.

q: Compliance wants to be able to search, export, and place a legal hold on the actual prompts and responses a specific user exchanged with Microsoft 365 Copilot last quarter. Is this possible, and if so, through what?
opts: No, Copilot interactions are ephemeral by design and are never written to any searchable log
Yes, Copilot prompts and responses are captured as audit events, searchable and exportable through Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Yes, but only by exporting chat transcripts manually from within the Copilot app itself
No, only Copilot Studio agent conversations are logged; Microsoft 365 Copilot chats are not recorded anywhere
why: Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses are captured as audit log events and are searchable, exportable, and placeable on legal hold through Purview eDiscovery, the same as other Microsoft 365 content. This makes Copilot interactions genuinely discoverable, not ephemeral or unlogged.

q: A marketing employee built a Copilot Studio agent that calls an unapproved file-storage connector and published it to Microsoft Teams, where other users can now find it. You must stop users from running the agent now and prevent any future agent from combining that connector with Microsoft 365 data, without affecting other agents. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
opts: Block the agent in the agent registry (Agents > All agents) in the Microsoft 365 admin center so users can no longer run it
Create a Power Platform data policy that places the connector in the Blocked group for the environment
Delete the Power Platform environment that hosts the agent so the agent can no longer be invoked
Turn off the Allow web search in Copilot policy in the Cloud Policy service
why: Blocking the agent in the agent registry removes it from users immediately, and a Power Platform data policy (formerly called a DLP policy) that classifies the connector as Blocked prevents any agent or flow in that environment from using it going forward. Deleting the environment would also remove every other agent and flow in it, violating the 'without affecting other agents' constraint. The Allow web search in Copilot policy controls whether Microsoft 365 Copilot can use public web results and has nothing to do with connectors.

q: To assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on through group-based licensing, the add-on must be assigned by the same group that assigns the user's base Microsoft 365 license.
opts: True
False
why: Group-based licensing evaluates each assignment independently; the add-on can be assigned by a dedicated pilot group while the base license comes from another group or from a direct assignment. The only requirement is that the user ends up with an eligible base license plus the add-on. Tying the two to one group is a common assumption that would force restructuring licensing groups unnecessarily.

q: A user who can open an encrypted document because the sensitivity label grants only the VIEW usage right can still have Microsoft 365 Copilot summarize that document.
opts: True
False
why: For encrypted content, Copilot returns it only if the user holds both the VIEW and EXTRACT usage rights. Content protected without the EXTRACT right (for example Do Not Forward) stays hidden from Copilot even though the user can open it. The misconception is treating 'the user can open the file' as 'Copilot can use the file'.

q: With Restricted SharePoint Search enabled, a user can still have Microsoft 365 Copilot reference a file from a site that is not on the allowed list if that file was shared directly with the user or the user recently opened it.
opts: True
False
why: Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) limits organization-wide search and Copilot grounding to the allowed sites, but it deliberately keeps content a user owns, has recently accessed, or has had shared directly with them discoverable, since the user already works with it. It is a visibility stopgap for broadly shared sites, not a per-file access control.

q: A Contoso tenant with Microsoft 365 E5 can start using Microsoft Security Copilot without separately provisioning Security Compute Units in Azure, because E5 includes a monthly SCU allotment.
opts: True
False
why: Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 include Security Copilot with a monthly allotment of 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 user licenses (up to 10,000), provisioned automatically with no Azure setup. Tenants without E5 or E7 still purchase provisioned SCUs, and in every case Security Copilot is separate from the per-user Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.

q: During a Copilot pilot, a Contoso user shows that Copilot summarized a salary spreadsheet. Investigation finds the file sits on an HR site that was shared with 'Everyone except external users', and the user had never opened it. Which two conclusions are correct? (Choose two.)
opts: The user already had permission to the file through the broad sharing grant; Copilot did not create new access
Remediation belongs in SharePoint: remove the broad grant and review the HR site's sharing settings
Copilot cached the spreadsheet from another user's session and served it across accounts
Disabling the Semantic Index for the HR site would have prevented the exposure
why: Copilot only surfaces what the requesting user can open, so the spreadsheet was reachable because of the 'Everyone except external users' grant, and the fix is to correct that sharing, which SharePoint Advanced Management's data access governance reports help find at scale. Copilot has no cross-user cache; each response is grounded for the requesting identity. The Semantic Index cannot be disabled per site; hiding a site from Copilot during review is done with Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery).

q: Contoso enables Data Security Posture Management for AI in Microsoft Purview. Which two outcomes can Contoso expect? (Choose two.)
opts: Reports showing sensitive information types detected in prompts and responses across Copilot and third-party AI sites
One-click recommended policies, such as a DLP policy that limits pasting sensitive data into AI websites
Automatic blocking of any Copilot response that contains sensitive information
A licensing prerequisite that must be satisfied before Copilot licenses can be assigned
why: DSPM for AI provides visibility reports on sensitive data in AI interactions and surfaces recommended policies it can create for you, which is how it bridges discovery to action. It does not itself enforce anything; blocking requires a DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location or endpoint DLP for AI sites. It is also not a licensing gate; Copilot licenses can be assigned whether or not DSPM for AI has ever been opened.

q: An admin wants to measure Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption across the organization — which apps it's used in and overall active-user trends — without being able to see the specific content of any individual user's prompts. Which capability should they use?
opts: A Microsoft Purview eDiscovery search across each named user's mailbox
Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard
Insider Risk Management case details for each licensed user
Restricted SharePoint Search reporting in the SharePoint admin center
why: Copilot usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard show aggregated adoption metrics like active users and app usage trends without exposing individual prompt content. Seeing a specific user's actual prompts would require an eDiscovery search instead, which is a different, more invasive capability.

q: A company has not purchased any Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses, yet an employee reports using "Copilot" to ask general web-grounded questions from within a Microsoft 365 app. What is the most likely explanation?
opts: The employee is using Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, included at no extra cost with a Microsoft Entra work account
The company must already have purchased Copilot add-on licenses previously without anyone realizing it
This isn't possible without a paid Copilot add-on license assigned to that specific user
The employee is actually using Microsoft Security Copilot, which is free for every licensed user
why: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is included with any Microsoft Entra work account at no extra licensing cost and provides web-grounded chat, distinct from the licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on that grounds answers in the organization's own Semantic Index. Security Copilot is a separate, SCU-billed product, not a free option for general use.

q: A custom Copilot Studio agent built by one department is consuming far more usage than its prepaid Copilot Credit capacity (formerly measured in messages) allows. What happens once that prepaid capacity is exhausted, assuming no additional capacity has been purchased?
opts: The agent is unpublished automatically and its owner must republish it once capacity is added
Further usage is billed pay-as-you-go if enabled; otherwise the agent may stop responding until the next period
Further usage is always billed pay-as-you-go automatically, with no setting required
The agent keeps running but is throttled to a slower service tier at no additional cost
why: Once prepaid Copilot Credit capacity (formerly messages) is exhausted, further Copilot Studio agent usage draws on metered pay-as-you-go billing if enabled, or the agent may stop responding until the next capacity period if it is not. Pay-as-you-go has to be enabled; it does not switch itself on, and the agent is neither deleted, unpublished nor moved to a free throttled tier. Monitoring capacity consumption matters because a heavily used agent can exhaust prepaid capacity quickly.

q: The EU Data Boundary is a Copilot-specific setting that only affects where Copilot prompts are processed, with no effect on other Microsoft 365 workloads.
opts: True
False
why: The EU Data Boundary is a tenant-wide data-residency commitment covering the storage and processing of Microsoft 365 data broadly, including but not limited to Copilot prompts, grounding data, and generated responses. It is not a narrow, Copilot-only toggle.

q: A Contoso employee publishes a Copilot Studio agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot, but colleagues cannot find it in their agent list. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
opts: If the tenant requires admin approval for agents, the agent remains unavailable until an admin approves it in the agent registry of the Microsoft 365 admin center
An admin can make the approved agent available to specific users or groups rather than to everyone
Publishing from Copilot Studio automatically makes the agent available to every user in the tenant
An admin must first create an app registration for the agent in Microsoft Entra before it can appear
why: Published agents flow through the agent registry (Agents > All agents) in the Microsoft 365 admin center, where tenants that require approval hold them until an admin acts, and the admin can then deploy the agent to all users, specific groups, or no one. Publishing alone does not grant tenant-wide availability, which is exactly why the colleagues cannot see it. Copilot Studio handles the agent's identity and registration as part of publishing; the admin does not hand-create an app registration.

q: Contoso has 1,000 employees with Microsoft 365 E3. All employees need web-grounded AI chat with enterprise data protection. Only the 100 managers need Copilot in Word, Excel, and Teams meetings grounded in organizational data. You need to minimize licensing cost. What should you do?
opts: Buy 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for the managers and rely on Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat for everyone else
Buy 1,000 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses so every employee has a consistent Copilot experience
Buy 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and 900 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat licenses
Upgrade all 1,000 employees to Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Copilot in the apps
why: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat comes with every Microsoft Entra work account at no additional cost and provides web-grounded chat with enterprise data protection, so only the managers need the paid add-on that embeds Copilot in the apps and grounds it in organizational data. Licensing all 1,000 overspends by 900 licenses. There is no separate Copilot Chat license to buy, and Microsoft 365 E5 does not include Microsoft 365 Copilot.

q: Contoso's support team wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to answer questions such as 'what is the status of ticket 4821' using live data from a third-party ticketing system, and to create new tickets on request. What should you build?
opts: A Copilot Studio agent with an action that calls the ticketing system's API
A Copilot connector that indexes the ticketing system's records
A Power Platform data policy that allows the ticketing system connector
A SharePoint list synchronized nightly from the ticketing system and an agent grounded on it
why: Live lookups and write-backs such as creating a ticket require an action (plugin) that calls the system's API at runtime, which is what a Copilot Studio agent with a connector action provides. A Copilot connector is the near-miss: it indexes a copy of the records for search and grounding, so answers can be stale and it cannot create tickets. A Power Platform data policy only permits or blocks connectors; it builds nothing. A nightly SharePoint sync is neither live nor capable of taking actions.

q: DSPM for AI reports show many interactions where Copilot surfaced files with an "Anyone in the organization" link that contain sensitive financial terms. The security team wants to move from just seeing this in reports to actually blocking Copilot from including that sensitive content in future responses. What's the necessary next step, and why doesn't DSPM for AI alone accomplish it?
opts: Create or tune a Purview DLP policy scoped to Microsoft 365 Copilot, because DSPM for AI reports on risk but does not enforce
Nothing further is needed, because DSPM for AI reports begin enforcing once a risk threshold is reached
Enable Insider Risk Management instead, because it is what actually blocks Copilot responses
Apply a sensitivity label to DSPM for AI itself, which extends its reporting into an enforcement policy
why: DSPM for AI is a discovery and reporting capability — it surfaces oversharing and sensitive-data risk in AI interactions, but a separate DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location is what actually enforces: a sensitivity-label condition keeps labeled content out of Copilot processing, and a sensitive-information-type condition blocks prompts that contain that data. Its reports don't self-escalate into enforcement, Insider Risk Management addresses user behavior risk rather than content-level blocking, and a sensitivity label can't be applied to DSPM for AI itself — it's a reporting tool, not a document.

q: A team wants to build a Copilot agent with its own independent reasoning engine and language model, entirely separate from Microsoft 365 Copilot's own orchestrator, trading simplicity for full control over its behavior. Which agent type are they building?
opts: A declarative agent
A custom engine agent
An agent created directly from a SharePoint site
A Copilot connector
why: A custom engine agent brings its own independent orchestrator and model, giving full control at the cost of far more development effort. A declarative agent and a SharePoint-grounded agent both build on Copilot's own existing orchestrator and Semantic Index instead, and a Copilot connector only indexes content for grounding rather than defining an agent's reasoning engine.

q: An admin wants to stop Copilot in Word from searching the public web for extra context, while leaving its ability to ground answers in the organization's own files and emails untouched. Where should this be configured?
opts: The EU Data Boundary configuration for the tenant's Microsoft 365 data
The Allow web search in Copilot policy, configured through the Cloud Policy service
A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location
Restricted SharePoint Search in the SharePoint admin center
why: The Allow web search in Copilot policy, configured through the Cloud Policy service (and reached from the Copilot page in the Microsoft 365 admin center), controls whether Copilot can search the public web while leaving grounding in organizational content alone. The EU Data Boundary governs data residency rather than web search, a DLP policy restricts sensitive content in responses rather than toggling web search, and Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) only hides sites that are not on its allowed list from search and Copilot, with no effect on web search.

q: A Contoso user asks Copilot to summarize a supplier's web page. Hidden text on the page instructs Copilot to email the user's recent documents to an external address. Copilot ignores the instruction and only summarizes the visible content. Which protection acted, and what class of attack was attempted?
opts: Built-in content safety and prompt shields, defending against cross-prompt injection
A DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location, defending against data exfiltration
Safe Links time-of-click scanning, defending against a malicious URL
Semantic Index permission trimming, defending against oversharing
why: Instructions hidden in grounding content that try to hijack the assistant are cross-prompt injection, and Microsoft 365 Copilot's content safety classifiers and prompt shields are the controls designed to detect and ignore them. A Copilot DLP policy filters sensitive content out of responses but does not recognize hidden instructions. Safe Links evaluates URL reputation when a user clicks, not what a page tells an AI to do. Permission trimming limits what Copilot can read, not how it responds to what it reads.

q: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location prevents cross-prompt injection attacks, because it inspects the grounding content that Copilot reads.
opts: True
False
why: Copilot DLP policies act on sensitive content: a sensitivity-label condition keeps labeled content out of Copilot processing, and a sensitive-information-type condition blocks prompts that contain that data; they do not look for hidden instructions or stop an injected prompt from steering the model. Cross-prompt injection is addressed by Copilot's built-in content safety and prompt-shielding protections. Conflating the two is treating a data-leak control as a manipulation control.

q: Contoso's HR agent in Copilot Studio must answer open-ended questions from a SharePoint policy library and must walk users through a fixed, scripted sequence when they request paid time off. Which two configurations support this design? (Choose two.)
opts: Enable generative orchestration so the agent picks the knowledge source or topic that best fits each message
Author a classic topic with trigger phrases and a scripted dialog for paid-time-off requests
Author a separate classic topic for every possible policy question in the SharePoint library
Switch the agent to classic orchestration only, because generative and classic cannot coexist in one agent
why: Generative orchestration lets the model route open-ended policy questions to the SharePoint knowledge source at runtime, while an explicitly authored topic keeps the PTO flow deterministic; the two coexist in the same agent. Authoring a topic per policy question is exactly the manual effort generative orchestration removes, and the claim that the two modes cannot coexist is false, because an agent can combine generative orchestration with authored topics.

q: A Copilot Studio agent needs to call both an approved internal line-of-business connector and a popular consumer social-media connector in the same action. The organization's Power Platform data policy places those two connectors in separate classification groups. What happens when the agent tries to combine them?
opts: The combination is blocked, because the two connectors fall into different classification groups in the Power Platform data policy
The combination succeeds, because Power Platform data policies apply only to Power Automate flows, not Copilot Studio agents
The combination succeeds, since Copilot Studio agents are automatically exempt from Power Platform data policy enforcement
The combination is blocked only when a separate Purview DLP policy scoped to Copilot interactions is also configured
why: Power Platform data policies (formerly DLP policies) group connectors into classifications and block connectors from different groups from being combined in the same flow or agent action, which is exactly what stops this combination. These policies apply broadly across Power Platform, including Copilot Studio agents, and this block does not depend on a separate Purview DLP policy scoped to Copilot interactions.

q: An admin needs to fully block a specific finance-only SharePoint site from being opened by anyone outside one designated security group, even by users who otherwise hold broad admin permissions. Which capability actually accomplishes this, as opposed to only hiding the site from search and Copilot?
opts: Restricted SharePoint Search applied to the finance site
Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management
A sensitivity label scoped to Files & emails applied to the site's documents
Data Security Posture Management for AI reporting
why: Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management actually limits who can access a site at all, unlike Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery), which only removes a site from search and Copilot results while leaving every existing permission untouched. A Files & emails-scoped sensitivity label protects individual documents rather than gating access to a whole site, and DSPM for AI only reports on risk rather than enforcing any access restriction.

q: Before a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout, an admin wants a prioritized list of SharePoint sites that are overshared or contain sensitive content, so remediation effort can focus on the highest-risk sites first. Which capability provides this site-level list?
opts: Data access governance reports in SharePoint Advanced Management
Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Compliance Manager assessment templates in Microsoft Purview
Content explorer in Microsoft Purview, used on its own
why: Data access governance reports are built specifically to surface overshared or sensitive SharePoint sites so remediation can be prioritized before a wider Copilot rollout. Usage reports measure Copilot adoption rather than site risk, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory requirements rather than SharePoint sharing risk, and Content explorer shows where labeled content currently sits without prioritizing sites by oversharing.

q: A team uses Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to draft a project brief, then wants several teammates to keep editing and refining that draft together over the next several days rather than losing it as a one-time chat reply. What should they turn the draft into?
opts: A Copilot Page
A Copilot Notebook
A new Teams channel post
A Teams meeting recap
why: A Copilot Page turns a chat response into a persistent, shareable canvas that several people can keep open and co-author over the following days. A Copilot Notebook gathers references and chats into a workspace for grounding further prompts; it is not the way to co-edit one drafted document. A channel post and a meeting recap are static outputs rather than live, co-authored drafts.

q: In Contoso's Teams meetings, participants speak English and Spanish. Contoso wants each participant to hear speech translated in real time, and wants live notes with action items captured during the meeting, using Microsoft-provided agents with no custom build. Which two agents should you enable? (Choose two.)
opts: Facilitator
Interpreter
Researcher
Analyst
why: Facilitator is the built-in meeting agent that keeps live notes and surfaces action items as the discussion happens, and Interpreter provides real-time speech translation in Teams meetings. Researcher performs multi-step research across work data and the web in Copilot Chat, and Analyst reasons over data and generates analysis; neither operates inside a live meeting.

q: Before assigning any Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses, an admin wants to know how exposed the organization currently is to oversharing and identity hygiene gaps, so problems can be fixed ahead of rollout rather than discovered afterward. Which activity addresses this stage specifically?
opts: Running a Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment
Reviewing Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports
Reviewing the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard
Running DSPM for AI reports after the first month of usage
why: A readiness assessment runs before rollout specifically to score factors like identity hygiene, device compliance, and oversharing risk so they can be addressed ahead of time. Usage reports and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard measure adoption after licenses are already assigned, and DSPM for AI reports on actual AI interactions, which requires usage to have already started.

q: An organization wants to require a compliant device specifically before Microsoft 365 Copilot sign-in succeeds, while leaving its existing sign-in requirements for the rest of Microsoft 365 unchanged. How should this be configured?
opts: Enabling security defaults, since it automatically applies stricter rules to Copilot only
A Conditional Access policy that targets the Enterprise Copilot Platform service principal as a cloud app
A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location, set to block users on unmanaged devices
The Allow web search in Copilot policy in Cloud Policy, applied to the users who need a compliant device
why: Because Microsoft 365 Copilot authenticates through the same Microsoft Entra sign-in as other Microsoft 365 apps, a Conditional Access policy can target its Enterprise Copilot Platform service principal (which may first need to be created so it appears in the app picker) as its own cloud app, layering a stricter device requirement onto Copilot sign-in without touching the rest of Microsoft 365. Security defaults apply one uncustomizable baseline to everything rather than singling out Copilot, a DLP policy governs content in responses rather than sign-in requirements, and the Allow web search in Copilot policy only controls whether Copilot searches the public web.

q: Content a user writes into a Copilot Page is a durable Microsoft 365 file, so it is within the scope of Purview eDiscovery, retention and audit.
opts: True
False
why: A Copilot Page is a durable file (new pages are stored in the user's OneDrive for Business, earlier ones in a SharePoint Embedded container), so eDiscovery, retention, and audit cover it like other Microsoft 365 content. The misconception is that because a Page is not an email or a chat message, it falls outside compliance tooling.

q: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location prevents a Copilot Studio agent from using a Non-Business connector in the same action as a Business connector.
opts: True
False
why: Connector grouping and combination rules are enforced by Power Platform data policies, which govern what a Copilot Studio agent, flow, or app is allowed to call. Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot governs sensitive content in Copilot interactions and has no concept of connector classification. The two are easy to confuse because Power Platform data policies were formerly called DLP policies, but they operate at different layers.

q: Contoso licenses SharePoint Advanced Management and finds 40 overshared sites before its Copilot rollout. Which two actions rely on SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities? (Choose two.)
opts: Run data access governance reports to find sites shared with 'Everyone except external users' and launch site access reviews
Apply restricted access control so only members of a Finance security group can access the Finance site
Enable Restricted SharePoint Search with an allowed list that leaves the 40 sites out of Copilot results
Create a DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location to keep labeled content out of responses
why: Data access governance reports and the site access reviews launched from them, together with restricted access control, are SharePoint Advanced Management features. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) is a tenant-level SharePoint setting that does not require the Advanced Management license, and a Copilot DLP policy is a Microsoft Purview capability; both help with a rollout but belong to different products.

q: A Microsoft 365 admin center article says users need the Microsoft Copilot license, while the AB-650 outline says Microsoft 365 Copilot. What is the relationship?
opts: Microsoft Copilot replaces Copilot Chat and removes the need for a separate add-on
Microsoft Copilot is the free consumer app and Microsoft 365 Copilot is the only work version
They are different SKUs that must both be assigned to a user
They are the same licensed experience, which Microsoft documentation now calls Microsoft Copilot
why: Microsoft renamed the Microsoft 365 Copilot experience to Microsoft Copilot (and Copilot Chat to Microsoft Copilot Chat), with no change to its security, compliance or privacy commitments. Admin center documentation also distinguishes the consumer version for personal accounts. The rename does not merge Copilot and Copilot Chat or require two licenses.

q: Which three-part structure describes the Copilot Control System (Copilot controls) framework?
opts: Plan, Deploy, and Adopt, as in the adoption lifecycle of a rollout
Discover, Protect, and Respond, as used in security operations playbooks
Identity, Devices, and Applications, with Microsoft Entra as the policy engine
Security and governance, Management controls and Measurement and reporting
why: Copilot controls are organized into Security and governance (data security, AI security, compliance), Management controls (licensing and metering, agent lifecycle, customization) and Measurement and reporting (readiness, productivity impact, business value). The other triples are generic frameworks or lists that do not match Microsoft's pillars.

q: An admin who holds only the AI Administrator role wants to change the tenant's Copilot AI disclaimer and the Copilot image generation setting. Is that role sufficient?
opts: No, they require the Teams Administrator role, because Copilot lives in Teams
Only the disclaimer; image generation needs the Power Platform Administrator
Yes, AI Administrator can change Copilot scenarios
No, both settings require the Global Administrator role in the Microsoft 365 admin center
why: AI Administrator can view and change Copilot scenarios under Copilot > Settings, and turning on the AI disclaimer specifically needs that role. Global Administrator is broader than necessary, and Teams or Power Platform roles apply to shortcuts that open those admin centers, not to these two settings.

q: Contoso wants to measure demand for Copilot without letting users commit the company to purchases. Which two settings or approaches fit? (Choose two.)
opts: Set Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases to Allow trials only
Review the Microsoft Copilot usage report to find licensed users who are not active
Disable group-based licensing so licenses cannot be assigned
Set self-service purchases to Allow so everyone can buy
why: Allow trials only lets users try Copilot for free without a path to purchase or automatic conversion, and the usage report's Enabled Users versus Active Users shows adoption among licensed users. Allow lets users buy, which defeats the purpose, and disabling group-based licensing has no bearing on demand measurement.

q: A user in the Contoso Finance group tells you she finds files from her own SharePoint sites and from a Salesforce connector in one place inside the Microsoft Copilot app. No admin set anything up. Which feature is this?
opts: Copilot Pages shared from Copilot Chat
Restricted SharePoint Search with Salesforce added to the allowed list of sites
Microsoft Copilot Search, using Copilot connectors for external data
A Copilot Studio agent with Salesforce configured as its knowledge source for answers
why: Copilot Search is a Search module in the Copilot app for licensed users, needs no admin setup and uses Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors to include external systems. Restricted SharePoint Search narrows visibility, Pages are collaborative canvases, and a Copilot Studio agent serves its own audience instead of providing tenant-wide search.

q: Contoso is in Germany and wants to know the default for Anthropic's Claude models in Microsoft Copilot for its tenant. What is accurate?
opts: They are on by default for every tenant everywhere, including tenants inside the EU Data Boundary
They are enabled automatically for each user as soon as a Copilot license is assigned
They cannot be enabled by any admin setting in the EU, because Microsoft blocks them there
Off by default in the EU, EFTA and UK, and admins can enable them under AI providers
why: Anthropic models are enabled by default for most commercial tenants but are disabled by default for EU/EFTA and UK tenants, where the AI providers setting shows No users until an admin opts in; they are excluded from the EU Data Boundary. They can be enabled, so claiming they cannot is wrong, and assigning a license does not switch them on.

q: Turning off the Anthropic model family in the Microsoft 365 admin center blocks users from using Copilot Cowork.
opts: True
False
why: Model settings control which models appear in the picker, not whether a user can use Cowork. Cowork access is granted by a spending policy that selects Cowork, and when Anthropic is off users keep working with the other models the organization allows.

q: The Cowork agent entry in Agents > All agents is blocked for the entire tenant, but several users with a spending policy that selects Cowork are still using it. Why?
opts: Those users all hold the Global Administrator role, which bypasses agent blocks
The block takes up to 24 hours to apply to existing sessions in the tenant
At general availability, only a spending policy that selects Cowork grants access
Spending policies override Conditional Access policies, so the block is ignored
why: For generally available Cowork, the agent-based access control used in preview is deprecated; the presence of a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork is the grant. Propagation delay or administrator status is not the reason, and spending policies do not override Conditional Access.

q: Contoso wants only a pilot group to use Cowork. A tenant-wide spending policy with a limit of 1 credit selects Cowork for All users, and a pilot policy selects it for the pilot group with a high limit. What is the result?
opts: Everyone is limited to 1 credit because the most restrictive policy wins
Every user in the tenant can use Cowork, and the pilot group gets the higher limit
Nobody can use Cowork until the two policies are merged
Only the pilot group can use Cowork, because the 1-credit policy blocks the others
why: A policy that selects Cowork grants access to everyone in its scope regardless of how small the limit is, so the All users policy gives everybody access. Precedence between overlapping policies only decides which limit applies, with the higher per-user limit used for pilot users. To restrict Cowork to the pilot group, remove Cowork from the tenant-wide policy.

q: An admin wants new Copilot services to be reviewed before users get access, rather than being included in existing spending policies automatically. What should be changed?
opts: Turn off Auto-apply new services on the spending policies
Remove all users from the default spending policy
Lower the monthly limit on each spending policy to zero
Disable the discovery setting for AI experiences
why: Auto-apply new services is enabled by default and automatically adds newly supported services and agents to a policy, so turning it off requires explicit review. A zero limit does not control the service list, removing users from the default policy affects current access, and the discovery setting controls visibility rather than policy membership.

q: In the Copilot usage report, 400 users are licensed and 300 tried a user-initiated Copilot feature in the last 28 days. Which value should the admin report as the active users rate?
opts: 300 prompts per user
25 percent
75 percent
133 percent
why: The active users rate is active users divided by enabled users, so 300 divided by 400 is 75 percent. 25 percent is the inactive share, prompts per user is a different metric, and a rate above 100 percent is not possible.

q: Leadership wants trends in productivity impact and user sentiment, compared with industry benchmarks, rather than a list of who is active. Which surface fits?
opts: The Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights
The Microsoft Copilot usage report in the admin center, filtered to the last 28 days
Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal
The Service health page of the admin center
why: The Copilot Dashboard presents readiness, adoption and impact, including sentiment from Pulse or Glint surveys and benchmark comparisons. The admin center usage report is operational and shows enablement and activity, Service health is about incidents, and Secure Score measures security posture.

q: An admin wants a single place to see every agent available to the organization, including those published by the company, shared by individual creators and built by Microsoft or partners. Where?
opts: The Copilot Studio environment list in the Power Platform admin center
Enterprise applications in the Microsoft Entra admin center
Agents > All agents > Registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Integrated apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center
why: The agent registry lists Microsoft agents, external partner-built agents, agents published by your org and agents shared by their creators in one inventory. The Integrated apps page is a separate area under Settings and is not the agent registry, enterprise applications show service principals rather than the agent inventory, and the Power Platform list covers only Copilot Studio environments.

q: Which agent registry card identifies agents created or managed outside Agent 365, so they lack its risk protection and observability?
opts: Agents without owners
Unmanaged agents
Pending update
Total agents
why: Unmanaged agents are those created or managed outside Agent 365. Agents without owners counts shared agents whose creator left, Total agents is the tenant-wide count, and Pending update is a request state, not a registry card.

q: A departing employee's account is hard-deleted, and the admin center now shows 14 shared agents without owners. What are appropriate admin actions?
opts: Re-create the deleted user account so the agents can be transferred back to it
Filter to ownerless agents, then block, delete or reassign them
Convert the agents to Copilot Studio agents so that a new owner can be assigned
Do nothing, because ownerless agents stop working by themselves once the creator is deleted
why: Ownerless shared agents can be filtered from the registry and then blocked, deleted or given a new owner, and a rule can reassign Agent Builder agents to the manager of the previous owner using the Entra hierarchy. They do not stop working by themselves, recreating a deleted user is unnecessary, and converting platforms does not solve the accountability gap.

q: A developer submitted an update to an existing published agent. What do users get until the admin approves the update?
opts: Both versions side by side
The new version in preview mode
The previous version of the agent
No access, because the agent is blocked during review
why: An update appears under Requests as Pending update, and until the admin selects Update in store users continue to use the previous version. The agent is not blocked or partly released during review.

q: Reviewing a Pending review request for a Copilot Studio agent, the admin wants to publish it to Finance only. Which two steps are part of the Publish to store wizard? (Choose two.)
opts: Choose a policy template and review the requested permissions, granting admin consent if appropriate
Select the users or groups that can install it, optionally including those who get it preinstalled
Re-author the agent's topics in Copilot Studio
Assign each user an Agent 365 license from the wizard
why: The wizard asks for the audience, optional preinstall audience, the policy template and a review of permissions with admin consent. Editing topics is the maker's job in Copilot Studio, and license assignment happens through licensing, not in the publishing wizard.

q: Contoso wants the company's agents and plugins to be installable by employees, but wants non-Microsoft agents from external publishers blocked. Where is this controlled?
opts: Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions
Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access, clearing external publishers
Agents > Settings > Sharing, choosing No users for organization-wide sharing
Copilot > Settings > Copilot AI disclaimer, adding an AI policy link
why: Agent and plugin access lets an admin allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft, by the organization and by external publishers independently. Sharing controls who may share Agent Builder agents broadly, the disclaimer is a display setting, and consent settings control app permissions rather than agent catalogs.

q: The Security Reader role can approve agent requests and change agent configurations in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
opts: True
False
why: Security Reader can view insights and the registry, but approving, installing and modifying agents is limited to Global Administrator and AI Administrator. Global Reader and AI Reader are read-only.

q: Contoso needs the same Entra, Purview, SharePoint and Defender protections applied to every agent it publishes, without configuring each product for each agent. What should the admin use?
opts: A Power Platform data policy configured separately in each environment
A separate sensitivity label created and assigned for each agent
A single Conditional Access policy that targets All cloud apps for every agent
An Agent 365 policy template applied at publish time or by a management rule
why: Policy templates bundle policies from Entra, Purview, SharePoint Online and Defender and can be applied at publish time or to existing agents in bulk. A label, a single Conditional Access policy or a connector data policy covers only one control surface.

q: A manager who is not an admin wants to review what her department's agent did during a session, including the trigger and tool calls. Where can she see it?
opts: The agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The Agent Activity tab in Teams, if she is the agent manager
Microsoft Defender advanced hunting in the security portal
The unified audit log search in Microsoft Purview
why: Users who interact with an agent or are assigned as its agent manager can view session activity in Teams or Copilot, while administrators monitor all agent activity in Defender. A regular manager has no access to hunting, the audit log or the admin center registry.

q: Contoso created an Agent 365 agent instance. Which protections apply to it automatically, and which need extra scoping?
opts: Everything applies automatically, including DLP, eDiscovery and Insider Risk Management policies
Audit and classification are automatic, while DLP and Insider Risk need policy scoping
Only Conditional Access applies, and Microsoft configures it automatically for every agent
Nothing applies until a dedicated sensitivity label is created for each agent instance
why: A new agent instance is enabled for auditing, sensitive data detection and the AI regulation assessments, but other solutions work only when the instance is included in the policies, as with a user. The rest of the options overstate or understate what is automatic.

q: In Microsoft Entra Agent ID, which relationship is required for every agent identity and blueprint to keep a business owner accountable?
opts: A guest owner in the partner tenant
At least one sponsor
A technical owner that is a group
A manager with Global Administrator
why: Sponsors are required, with at least one per agent identity and blueprint, to hold business accountability for purpose and lifecycle. Owners are optional and cannot be groups, and managers are not required to hold any admin role.

q: Contoso's fleet of 80 support agents needs the same Graph application permission and group membership, with approval and time-bound expiration. Which feature should the admin use?
opts: An entitlement management access package for agents
A SharePoint site role assignment through an access package
An access review of the Global Administrator role
A custom Conditional Access policy that grants the permission
why: Access packages for agents bundle group memberships, directory roles and OAuth API permissions with approval and expiration, so the access is intentional and auditable. SharePoint site roles cannot be added for agent identities, Conditional Access governs token issuance rather than granting permission, and an access review of an admin role is a different task.

q: An agent signs in to a resource by using its own agent identity with no user present. Which subject should a Conditional Access policy for this scenario target?
opts: The users and groups of the people who built it
The agent registry
The agent's user account
The agent identity or its blueprint
why: For application-only (autonomous) access the token subject is the agent identity, so the policy targets that identity or its blueprint. Targeting users covers on-behalf-of access, and a policy aimed at the agent's user account does not apply to the agent identity.

q: When the sponsor of 30 agent identities moves to another department, which Lifecycle Workflows task transfers accountability to the sponsor's manager?
opts: Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager
Disable user account and block sign-in
Remove user from all groups and teams
Send email to cosponsors about sponsor changes
why: The transfer task reassigns agent identity sponsorships to the manager and is available in mover and leaver workflows. Sending an email only notifies, and disabling or group removal do not move sponsorships.
